title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 51 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 390–398 (Night 51, continuing directly from nights-50), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 51 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Sharkān brings Princess Abrīza home to Baghdad; the king learns that she is the daughter of the king of the Rūm, and the three beads are shown to him. Sharkān discovers he has a half-brother and sister, Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Nuzhat al-Zamān, and burns with resentment. The king, infatuated with Abrīza, drugs her with bhang on his wazir Dandān's advice and takes her by force. She conceals her pregnancy, flees with her maid Marjāna and a black slave, al-Ghaḍbān, and, as the night breaks off at dawn, he turns on her. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْحَادِيَةُ وَالْخَمْسُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-ḥādiyatu wa-al-khamsūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the first-and-fifty,
sentences.i: And when it was the fifty-first night,
sentences.n: الْحَادِيَةُ is the ordinal "first" (literally "the one that joins"); with الْخَمْسُونَ it makes "the first and fiftieth", that is, the fifty-first. The print has the nominative ending -ūna on the tens, and we point it as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ شَرْكَانَ أَمَرَ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَةَ وَجَوَارِيَهَا أَنْ يَنْزِعْنَ مَا عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنَ الثِّيَابِ وَأَنْ يَلْبَسْنَ لِبْسَ بَنَاتِ الرُّومِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Sharkāna amara al-malikata Abrīzata wa-jawāriyahā an yanziʿna mā ʿalayhinna mina al-thiyābi wa-an yalbasna libsa banāti al-Rūmi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy, that Sharkān commanded the queen Abrīza and her girls that they strip off what is upon them of the garments, and that they wear the wearing of the daughters of Rūm.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Sharkān bade Queen Abrīza and her maids take off the clothes they wore and dress as the daughters of the Rūm dress.
sentences.n: السَّعِيدُأَنَّ is printed as one word: al-saʿīd ("the fortunate") run together with anna ("that"); we point it as two words glued, as the archive gives no space. أَنْ يَنْزِعْنَ and أَنْ يَلْبَسْنَ are feminine plural subjunctives (the -na ending is the same in the subjunctive), since the women are the subject. بَنَات الرُّوم are the Byzantine Greek women; الرُّوم are the Byzantines.

sentences.t: وَفَعَلْنَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-faʿalna dhālika
sentences.l: And they did that.
sentences.i: And they did so.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَرْسَلَ جَمَاعَةً مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ إِىَ بَغْدَادَ لِيُعْلِمَ وَالِدَهُ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ بِقُدُومِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu arsala jamāʿatan min aṣḥābihi iya Baghdāda li-yuʿlima wālidahu ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni bi-qudūmihi
sentences.l: Then that he sent a company of his companions to Baghdad, so that he might make-know his father ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān of his arrival,
sentences.i: Then he sent a party of his companions to Baghdad, to let his father, ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, know of his coming,
sentences.n: اى is printed where إِلَى, "to", is meant, with the lām dropped; we point the printed letters. ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ is a stock narrative "then he".

sentences.t: وَيُخْبِرَهُ أَنَّ صُحْبَتَهُ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَةَ ابْنَةَ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ لِيُرْسِلَ لَهَا مَنْ يُلَاقِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-yukhbirahu anna ṣuḥbatahu al-malikata Abrīzata ibnata al-maliki Ḥardūba maliki al-Rūmi li-yursila lahā man yulāqīhā
sentences.l: and tell him that in-his-company is the queen Abrīza, daughter of the king Ḥardūb, king of Rūm, so that he might send to her one who would meet her.
sentences.i: and to tell him that Queen Abrīza, daughter of King Ḥardūb, the king of the Rūm, was in his company, so that he might send someone to meet her.
sentences.n: The clause continues the purpose of the previous unit (لِيُعْلِمَ ... وَيُخْبِرَهُ). صُحْبَتَهُ is pointed as an accusative adverb, "in his company", with الْمَلِكَةَ in the accusative after أَنَّ, as the word order suggests.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ نَزَلُوا مِنْ سَاعَتِهِمْ وَوَقْتِهِمْ فِى الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي وَصَلُوا إِلَيْهِ وَنَزَلَ شَرْكَانُ وَبَاتُوا إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum nazalū min sāʿatihim wa-waqtihim fī al-makāni alladhī waṣalū ilayhi wa-nazala Sharkānu wa-bātū ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: Then that they alighted from their hour and their time in the place which they had reached, and Sharkān alighted, and they spent-the-night until the morning.
sentences.i: Then they halted at that very hour and moment in the place they had reached, and Sharkān dismounted, and they passed the night until morning.
sentences.n: مِنْ سَاعَتِهِمْ وَوَقْتِهِمْ, "from their hour and their time", means "at once, on the spot".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِالصَّبَاحِ رَكِبَ شَرْكَانُ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa Allāhu taʿālā bi-al-ṣabāḥi rakiba Sharkānu huwa wa-man maʿahu
sentences.l: And when God, exalted-is-He, brought-to-morning with the morning, Sharkān mounted, he and whoever was with him,
sentences.i: And when God Most High brought on the morning, Sharkān mounted, he and those with him,
sentences.n: أَصْبَحَ is normally intransitive ("to enter the morning"); with اللَّهُ as subject and بِالصَّبَاحِ, "with the morning", it is a stock phrase meaning that God caused the day to dawn. The invocation تَعَالَى ("exalted is He") follows God's name.

sentences.t: وَرَكِبَتْ أَيْضًا الْمَلِكَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ وَمَنْ مَعَهَا مِنَ الْجَيْشِ وَاسْتَقْبَلُوا الْمَدِينَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-rakibat aydan al-malikatu Abrīzatu wa-man maʿahā mina al-jayshi wa-istaqbalū al-madīnata
sentences.l: and the queen Abrīza also mounted, and whoever was with her of the army, and they faced the city.
sentences.i: and Queen Abrīza mounted too, with those of the army who were with her, and they made for the city.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ قَدْ أَقْبَلَ فِي أَلْفِ فَارِسٍ مِنْ أَجْلِ مُلَاقَاةِ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ هِيَ وَشَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-wazīri Dandāna qad aqbala fī alfi fārisin min ajli mulāqāti al-malikati Abrīzata hiya wa-Sharkāna
sentences.l: And when, behold, the vizier Dandān had come forward with a thousand horsemen, for the sake of meeting the queen Abrīza, she and Sharkān,
sentences.i: And behold, the vizier Dandān came riding up with a thousand horsemen to meet Queen Abrīza and Sharkān,
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِالْوَزِيرِ: the بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what appears, "and behold, the vizier". The pronoun هِيَ stands in apposition to the genitive الْمَلِكَةِ, "the queen, she", and the sentence then adds Sharkān.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ خَرَجُوا بِإِشَارَةِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ إِلَى مُلَاقَاتِهِمَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad kharajū bi-ishārati al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni ilā mulāqātihimā
sentences.l: and they had gone out at the sign of the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān to the meeting of them both.
sentences.i: having set out at the order of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān to meet them both.
sentences.n: إِشَارَة is literally a "sign" or "gesture" and here means a royal order.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبُوا مِنْهُمَا تَوَجَّهُوا إِلَيْهِمَا وَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qarubū minhumā tawajjahū ilayhimā wa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhimā
sentences.l: And when they drew near to them both, they turned toward them both, and kissed the earth between their two hands.
sentences.i: When they drew near, they went up to them and kissed the ground before them.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, "between his two hands", is the usual way to say "before him, in his presence"; kissing the ground is the sign of homage to a ruler.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَكِبَا وَرَكِبُوا مَعَهُمَا وَسَارُوا فِي خِدْ مَتِهِمَا حَتَّى دَخَلَا الْمَدِينَةَ وَطَلَعَا الْقَصْرَ
sentences.tr: thumma rakibā wa-rakibū maʿahumā wa-sārū fī khid matihimā ḥattā dakhalā al-madīnata wa-ṭalaʿā al-qaṣra
sentences.l: Then the two mounted, and they mounted with them both, and went in their service until the two entered the city and went-up the palace.
sentences.i: Then the two of them mounted, and the others rode with them in their service until they entered the city and went up to the palace.
sentences.n: خِدْ مَتِهِمَا is printed with a space inside the word; it is خِدْمَتِهِمَا, "their service", and we point the two printed pieces. طَلَعَا الْقَصْرَ takes the palace as a direct object, "went up (into) the palace".

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ شَرْكَانُ عَلَى وَالِدِهِ فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ وَاعْتَنَقَهُ وَسَأَلَهُ عَنِ الْخَبَرِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala Sharkānu ʿalā wālidihi fa-qāma ilayhi wa-iʿtanaqahu wa-saʾalahu ʿani al-khabari
sentences.l: And Sharkān entered upon his father, and he rose to him, and embraced him, and asked him about the news.
sentences.i: Sharkān went in to his father, who rose to him and embraced him and asked him for his news.
sentences.n: دَخَلَ عَلَى is "to go in to (someone's presence)". The أ in وَسَأَلَهُ is printed by the edition, so it stays as a full letter.

sentences.t: فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِمَا قَالَتْهُ الْمَلِكَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ وَمَا اتَّفَقَ لَهُ مَعَهَا وَكَيْفَ فَارَقَتْ مَمْلَكَتَهَا وَفَارَقَتْ أَبَاهَا
sentences.tr: fa-akhbarahu bi-mā qālathu al-malikatu Abrīzatu wa-mā ittafaqa lahu maʿahā wa-kayfa fāraqat mamlakatahā wa-fāraqat abāhā
sentences.l: And he informed him of what the queen Abrīza had said, and what had befallen him with her, and how she had left her kingdom and left her father.
sentences.i: He told him all that Queen Abrīza had said, and what had passed between himself and her, and how she had left her kingdom and her father.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّهَا اخْتَارَتِ الرَّحِيلَ مَعَنَا وَالْقُعُودَ عِنْدَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu innahā ikhtārati al-raḥīla maʿanā wa-al-quʿūda ʿindanā
sentences.l: And he said to him: Indeed she has chosen the departing with us and the sitting with us.
sentences.i: And he said to him, "She has chosen to leave with us and to stay with us,

sentences.t: وَإِنَّ مَلِكَ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ أَرَادَأَنْ يَعْمَلَ لَنَا حِيلَةً مِنْ أَجْلِ ابْنَتِهِ صَفِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: wa-inna malika al-Quṣṭanṭīniyyati arāda an yaʿmala lanā ḥīlatan min ajli ibnatihi Ṣafiyyata
sentences.l: And indeed the king of Constantinople wanted to do for us a trick, for the sake of his daughter Ṣafiyya,
sentences.i: And the king of Constantinople meant to play us a trick on account of his daughter Ṣafiyya,
sentences.n: أَرَادَأَنْ is printed as one word, arāda ("he wanted") run together with an ("that"); we point it as two words glued. حِيلَة is a ruse or stratagem.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ مَلِكَ الرُّومِ قَدْ أَخْبَرَهُ بِحِكَايَتِهَا وَسَبَبِ إِهْدَائِهَا إِلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: li-anna malika al-Rūmi qad akhbarahu bi-ḥikāyatihā wa-sababi ihdāʾihā ilayka
sentences.l: because the king of Rūm had informed him of her story and the cause of her being-gifted to you.
sentences.i: because the king of the Rūm had told him her story and the reason she was sent to you as a gift.
sentences.n: The pronoun "her" is Ṣafiyya, the daughter just mentioned, who was sent to ʿUmar as a gift. The ئ in إِهْدَائِهَا is printed by the edition and stays as a full letter.

sentences.t: وَإِنَّ مَلِكَ الرُّومِ مَا كَانَ يَعْرِفُ أَنَّهَا ابْنَةُ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-inna malika al-Rūmi mā kāna yaʿrifu annahā ibnatu al-maliki Afrīdūna maliki al-Quṣṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: And indeed the king of Rūm was not knowing that she was the daughter of the king Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople,
sentences.i: and the king of the Rūm did not know that she was the daughter of King Afrīdūn, the king of Constantinople;
sentences.n: The "she" is Ṣafiyya, not Abrīza. The negative مَا كَانَ يَعْرِفُ ("was not knowing") is a Middle Arabic way of saying "did not know"; مَا before a perfect or kāna-construction is the colloquial negative.

sentences.t: وَلَوْكَانَ يَعْرِفُ ذَلِكَ مَا كَانَ أَهْدَاهَا إِلَيْكَ بَلْ كَانَ يَرُدُّهَا إِلَى وَالِدِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-law kāna yaʿrifu dhālika mā kāna ahdāhā ilayka bal kāna yarudduhā ilā wālidihā
sentences.l: and if he had known that, he would not have gifted her to you, but would have been returning her to her father.
sentences.i: had he known it, he would not have given her to you as a gift, but would have sent her back to her father."
sentences.n: وَلَوْكَانَ is printed as one word, wa-law ("and if") run together with kāna; we point it as two words glued. The second kāna before يَرُدُّهَا gives "would have been returning", a past-habitual or conditional sense.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ شَرْكَانُ لِوَالِدِهِ وَلَا كَانَ خَلَاصُنَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمُورِ إِلَّا بِسَبَبِ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla Sharkānu li-wālidihi wa-lā kāna khalāṣunā min hādhihi al-umūri illā bi-sababi hādhihi al-jāriyati Abrīzata
sentences.l: Then Sharkān said to his father: And not was our deliverance from these affairs except by the cause of this girl Abrīza,
sentences.i: Then Sharkān said to his father, "Our deliverance from these troubles came only through this girl Abrīza,
sentences.n: وَلَا كَانَ is awkward as printed; it may stand for وَلَوْلَا ("and had it not been for"), but it reads sensibly as "and not was our deliverance ... except through", which is how we take it.

sentences.t: وَمَا رَأَيْنَا أَشْجَعَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-mā raʾaynā ashjaʿa minhā
sentences.l: and we have not seen any braver than her
sentences.i: and we have never seen anyone braver than she."
sentences.n: The speech continues in the next line of the print, so this unit is a fragment. The أ in رَأَيْنَا is printed by the edition and stays as a full letter.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ شَرَعَ يَحْكِي لِأَبِيهِ فِيمَا وَقَعَ لَهُ مِنْهَا مِنْ أَوَّلِ الْأَمْرِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمُصَارَعَةِ وَالْمُبَارَزَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu sharaʿa yaḥkī li-abīhi fī-mā waqaʿa lahu minhā min awwali al-amri ilā ākhirihi min amri al-muṣāraʿati wa-al-mubārazati
sentences.l: Then that he began to recount to his father in-what befell him from her, from the first of the matter to its last: of the matter of the wrestling and the single-combat.
sentences.i: Then he began to tell his father all that had passed between himself and her, from beginning to end: the wrestling and the duelling.
sentences.n: The unit opens in the middle of a sentence begun in the unit just before it. The last two phrases are in apposition to "the matter", spelling out what that matter was: the wrestling bout and the duel.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ مِنْ وَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَظُمَتْ أَبْرِيزَةُ عِنْدَهُ وَصَارَ يَتَمَنَّى أَنَّهُ يَرَاهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni min waladihi Sharkāna dhālika ʿaẓumat Abrīzatu ʿindahu wa-ṣāra yatamannā annahu yarāhā
sentences.l: And when ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān heard from his son Sharkān that, Abrīza grew-great in his presence, and he became wishing that he see her.
sentences.i: When King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān heard all this from his son Sharkān, Abrīza rose greatly in his esteem, and he began to long to see her.
sentences.n: عِنْدَهُ, literally "at him", means "in his view, in his regard". The main clause follows the long subordinate clause with no connective, which is ordinary Arabic sentence building.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ طَلَبَهَا أَنْ يَسْأَلَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu ṭalabahā an yasʾalahā
sentences.l: Then that he sought her, that he ask her.
sentences.i: Then he sent for her, to question her.
sentences.n: طَلَبَهَا is "he sought/demanded her" and means he asked for her to be brought. The print has أ in يَسْأَلَهَا.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ ذَهَبَ شَرْكَانُ إِلَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ يَدْعُوكِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika dhahaba Sharkānu ilayhā wa-qāla lahā inna al-malika yadʿūki
sentences.l: And at that Sharkān went to her and said to her: Indeed the king calls you.
sentences.i: At that Sharkān went to her and said, "The king summons you."
sentences.n: The print leaves the final كاف of يَدْعُوك bare; since a woman is addressed we point the feminine ـكِ.

sentences.t: فَأَجَابَتْ بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ajābat bi-al-samʿi wa-al-ṭāʿati
sentences.l: And she answered with the hearing and the obedience.
sentences.i: She answered with hearing and obedience.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهَا شَرْكَانُ وَأَتَى بِهَا إِلَى وَالِدِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahā Sharkānu wa-atā bihā ilā wālidihi
sentences.l: And Sharkān took her and came with her to his father.
sentences.i: Sharkān took her and brought her to his father.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْمَلِكُ قَاعِدًا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ وَأَخْرَجَ مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ أَهْلِ دَوْلَتِهِ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ عِنْدَهُ غَيْرُ الْخَدَمِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-maliku qāʿidan ʿalā kursiyyihi wa-akhraja man kāna ʿindahu min ahli dawlatihi wa-lam yabqa ʿindahu ghayru al-khadami
sentences.l: And the king was sitting upon his chair, and had-put-out whoever was with him of the people of his state, and there did not remain with him other-than the servants.
sentences.i: The king was seated on his throne. He had sent out all who were with him of the people of his court, so that none remained with him but the servants.
sentences.n: The shadda on the yā' of كُرْسِيِّهِ is printed in the edition and kept. The perfect أَخْرَجَ after وَكَانَ is read as a pluperfect ("had sent out").

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ وَقَبَّلَتِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَتَرْجَمَتْ بِحُسْنِ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalati al-jāriyatu Abrīzatu wa-qabbalati al-arḍa bayna yadayi al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni wa-tarjamat bi-ḥusni al-kalāmi
sentences.l: And the girl Abrīza entered, and kissed the earth between the two hands of the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān, and spoke-out with goodness of speech.
sentences.i: The girl Abrīza came in, kissed the ground before King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and addressed him in fair and gracious words.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيِ is the usual "in front of, in the presence of". تَرْجَمَ here means "to expound, to speak out", not "translate". The print writes يدى with an undotted final letter, which we read as يَدَيِ.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْمَلِكُ مِنْ فَصَاحَتِهَا وَشَكَرَهَا عَلَى مَا فَعَلَتْ مَعَ وَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ وَأَمَرَهَا بِالْجُلُوسِ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-maliku min faṣāḥatihā wa-shakarahā ʿalā mā faʿalat maʿa waladihi Sharkāna wa-amarahā bi-al-julūsi
sentences.l: And the king marvelled at her eloquence, and thanked her for what she had done with his son Sharkān, and commanded her with the sitting.
sentences.i: The king marvelled at her eloquence and thanked her for what she had done for his son Sharkān, and bade her be seated.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَتْ وَكَشَفَتْ عَنْ وَجْهِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-jalasat wa-kashafat ʿan wajhihā
sentences.l: And she sat, and uncovered from her face.
sentences.i: She sat down and unveiled her face.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَهَا الْمَلِكُ طَارَ عَقْلُهُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā al-maliku ṭāra ʿaqluhu min raʾsihi
sentences.l: And when the king saw her, his mind flew from his head.
sentences.i: When the king saw her, his wits flew from his head.
sentences.n: The print writes رأها with the hamza on the alif and no madda (Classical رَآهَا); we point it raʾāhā. "His mind flew from his head" is the stock expression for being struck senseless with love or wonder.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَرَّبَهَا إِلَيْهِ وَأَدْنَاهَا وَأَفْرَدَ لَهَا قَصْرًا مُخْتَصًّا بِهَا وَبِجَوَارِيهَا وَرَتَّبَ لَهَا وَلِجَوَارِيهَا الرَّوَاتِبَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qarrabahā ilayhi wa-adnāhā wa-afrada lahā qaṣran mukhtaṣṣan bihā wa-bi-jawārīhā wa-rattaba lahā wa-li-jawārīhā al-rawātiba
sentences.l: Then that he brought her near to him and drew her close, and set-apart for her a palace, made-exclusive to her and to her girls, and appointed for her and for her girls the stipends.
sentences.i: Then he drew her close to him, and set apart a palace for her and her maids alone, and appointed allowances for her and for her maids.
sentences.n: The shadda on مُخْتَصًّا is printed in the edition and kept. الرَّوَاتِب are the regular allowances (rations and pay) fixed for a person.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ يَسْأَ لَهَا عَلَى تِلْكَ الْخَرَزَاتِ الثَّلٰثِ الَّتِي تَقَدَّمَ ذِكْرُهَا فَقَالَتْ لَهُ هَاهِيَ مَعِي يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha yasʾa lahā ʿalā tilka al-kharazāti al-thalāthi allatī taqaddama dhikruhā fa-qālat lahu hāhiya maʿī yā malika al-zamāni
sentences.l: Then he took to asking her about those beads, the three, which its mention preceded; and she said to him: Here-it-is with me, O king of the time.
sentences.i: Then he began to ask her about those three beads that were mentioned before, and she said to him, "Here they are, with me, O king of the age."
sentences.n: The print splits يسألها into two words, يسأ لها ("asks her"); we keep the printed gap. الثَّلٰثِ is the print's spelling ثلث for ثلاث (three), with the dagger alif supplied. هَاهِيَ, "here she is", uses the feminine singular, which agrees with خَرَزَات, a plural of a thing. The "three beads" are the ones the narrative has already brought up.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا قَامَتْ وَمَضَتْ إِلَى مَحَلِّهَا وَفَتَحَتْ حَوَائِجَهَا وَأَخْرَجَتْ مِنْهَا عُلْبَةً وَأَخْرَجَتْ مِنَ الْعُلْبَةِ حُقًّا مِنَ الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā qāmat wa-maḍat ilā maḥallihā wa-fataḥat ḥawāʾijahā wa-akhrajat minhā ʿulbatan wa-akhrajat mina al-ʿulbati ḥuqqan mina al-dhahabi
sentences.l: Then that she rose and went to her place, and opened her belongings, and brought out from them a box, and brought out from the box a casket of the gold.
sentences.i: Then she rose and went to her own quarters, opened her baggage, took out a box, and from the box took out a casket of gold.
sentences.n: The shadda on حُقًّا is printed in the edition and kept. حَوَائِج are belongings or necessaries, here her baggage.

sentences.t: وَفَتَحَتْ وَأَخْرَجَتْ مِنْهُ تِلْكَ الْخَرَزَاتِ الثَّلٰثِ وَبَاسَتْهَا وَأَعْطَتْهَا لِلْمَلِكِ وَانْصَرَفَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-fataḥat wa-akhrajat minhu tilka al-kharazāti al-thalāthi wa-bāsathā wa-aʿṭathā li-al-maliki wa-inṣarafat
sentences.l: And she opened, and brought out from it those beads, the three, and kissed them, and gave them to the king, and departed.
sentences.i: She opened it, took out the three beads, kissed them, gave them to the king, and withdrew.
sentences.n: وَفَتَحَتْ has no stated object; it means the casket just mentioned. بَاسَتْهَا is from بَاسَ, "to kiss", a form more usual in Middle Arabic than Classical قَبَّلَتْهَا.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْ قَلْبَهُ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhat qalbahu maʿahā
sentences.l: And she took his heart with her.
sentences.i: And she carried his heart away with her.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ انْصِرَافِهَا أَرْسَلَ إِلَى وَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ فَحَضَرَ فَأَعْطَاهُ خَرَزَةً مِنْ ثَلٰثِ خَرَزَاتٍ فَسَأَلَهُ عَنِ الِاثْنَيْنِ الْأُخْرَيَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda inṣirāfihā arsala ilā waladihi Sharkāna fa-ḥaḍara fa-aʿṭāhu kharazatan min thalāthi kharazātin fa-saʾalahu ʿani al-ithnayni al-ukhrayayni
sentences.l: And after her departing he sent to his son Sharkān, and he came; and he gave him a bead from three beads, and asked him about the two, the other-two.
sentences.i: After she had gone he sent for his son Sharkān, who came; and he gave him one bead of the three and asked him about the other two.
sentences.n: الْأُخْرَيَيْنِ is the oblique dual of أُخْرَى, "other"; the print spells it with two yā's. ثَلٰثِ is the print's ثلث for ثلاث.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا وَلَدِي قَدْ أَعْطَيْتُ مِنْهُمَا وَاحِدَةً لِأَخِيكَ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَالْأُخْرَى لِنُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ أُخْتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā waladī qad aʿṭaytu minhumā wāḥidatan li-akhīka Ḍawʾi al-Makāni wa-al-ukhrā li-Nuzhati al-Zamāni ukhtika
sentences.l: And he said: O my child, I have given, of the two, one to your brother Light-of-the-Place, and the other to Delight-of-the-Age, your sister.
sentences.i: He said, "My son, I have given one of the two to your brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and the other to your sister Nuzhat al-Zamān."
sentences.n: ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ ("Light of the Place") and نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ ("Delight of the Age") are proper names, each a two-part construct.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ أَنَّ لَهُ أَخًا يُسَمَّى ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَمَاكَانَ يَعْرِفُ إِلَّا أُخْتَهُ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى وَالِدِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَلَكَ وَلَدٌ غَيْرِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Sharkānu anna lahu akhan yusammā Ḍawʾa al-Makāni wa-mākāna yaʿrifu illā ukhtahu Nuzhata al-Zamāni iltafata ilā wālidihi wa-qāla lahu ayyuhā al-maliku a-laka waladun ghayrī
sentences.l: And when Sharkān heard that to him was a brother called Light-of-the-Place, and he had not been knowing except his sister Delight-of-the-Age, he turned to his father and said to him: O king, is-there to-you a child other-than-me?
sentences.i: When Sharkān heard that he had a brother named Ḍawʾ al-Makān (he had known of no one but his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān), he turned to his father and said, "O king, have you another child besides me?"
sentences.n: وَمَاكَانَ is printed as one word, for وَمَا كَانَ. The print has الك for أَلَكَ (the question particle أَ plus لَكَ, "have you"), with the hamza unwritten.

sentences.t: قَالَ نَعَمْ وَعُمْرُهُ الْآنَ سِتُّ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: qāla naʿam wa-ʿumruhu al-āna sittu sinīna
sentences.l: He said: Yes, and his age now is six years.
sentences.i: "Yes," said the king, "and he is now six years old."
sentences.n: سِنِينَ keeps the oblique ـِينَ ending in a place where Classical Arabic would use a different construction for a numeral; it is a Middle Arabic pattern. The آ of الْآنَ is printed by the edition.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعْلَمَهُ أَنَّ اسْمَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَأُخْتَهُ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَأَنَّهُمَا وُلِدَا فِي بَطْنٍ وَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: thumma aʿlamahu anna ismahu Ḍawʾu al-Makāni wa-ukhtahu Nuzhatu al-Zamāni wa-annahumā wulidā fī baṭnin wāḥidin
sentences.l: Then he informed him that his name was Light-of-the-Place, and his sister Delight-of-the-Age, and that the two of them were born in one belly.
sentences.i: Then he told him that the boy's name was Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his sister's Nuzhat al-Zamān, and that the two had been born of one womb.
sentences.n: "In one belly" is the Arabic idiom for twins.

sentences.t: فَصَعُبَ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ وَلَكِنَّهُ كَتَمَ سِرَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣaʿuba ʿalayhi dhālika wa-lākinnahu katama sirrahu
sentences.l: And that was hard upon him, but he hid his secret.
sentences.i: This weighed heavily on him, but he kept his feelings to himself.
sentences.n: سِرَّهُ, "his secret", is what is hidden in the heart. The shadda on the rāʾ is printed and kept.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِوَالِدِهِ عَلَى بَرَكَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-wālidihi ʿalā barakati Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And he said to his father: Upon the blessing of God, exalted-is-He.
sentences.i: and said to his father, "In the blessing of God Most High."
sentences.n: A short wish or acceptance formula with the verb left out: "let it be on God's blessing", meaning "so be it, and God bless it".

sentences.t: وَرَمَى الْخَرَزَةَ مِنْ يَدِهِ وَنَفَضَ أَثْوَا بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ramā al-kharazata min yadihi wa-nafaḍa athwā bihi
sentences.l: And he threw the bead from his hand and shook his garments.
sentences.i: He threw the bead from his hand and shook out his clothes.
sentences.n: The print splits اثوابه into اثوا به; we keep the printed gap, reading أَثْوَابِهِ "his garments". Shaking out the clothes is a gesture of throwing off a matter or a burden.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ مَالِي أَرَاكَ قَدْ تَغَيَّرَتْ أَحْوَالُكَ لَمَّا سَمِعْتَ هَذَا الْخَبَرَ مَعَ أَنَّكَ صَاحِبُ الْمَمْلَكَةِ مِنْ بَعْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku mālī arāka qad taghayyarat aḥwāluka lammā samiʿta hādhā al-khabara maʿa annaka ṣāḥibu al-mamlakati min baʿdī
sentences.l: And the king said to him: What is to me, I see you, your states have changed, when you heard this report, along with that you are the master of the kingdom after me?
sentences.i: The king said to him, "What is the matter, that I see you so changed since you heard this news, when you are to be master of the kingdom after me?"
sentences.n: مَالِي أَرَاكَ is "what ails me that I see you...": مَا لِي with the following verb as a circumstantial clause. أَحْوَال, plural of حَال, is the condition of a person, here his bearing and looks. مَعَ أَنَّكَ is "although".

sentences.t: وَقَدْ حَلَّفْتُ لَكَ الْجَيْشَ وَعَاهَدْتُ أُمَرَاءَ الدَّوْلَةِ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَهَذِهِ خَرَزَةٌ لَكَ مِنْ ثَلٰثِ خَرَزَاتٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ḥallaftu laka al-jayša wa-ʿāhadtu umarāʾa al-dawlati ʿalā dhālika wa-hādhihi kharazatun laka min thalāthi kharazātin
sentences.l: And I have made-swear for you the army, and made-covenant with the emirs of the state upon that; and this is a bead for you from three beads.
sentences.i: I have had the army swear allegiance to you, and bound the emirs of the realm to it. And here is a bead for you, one of the three.
sentences.n: حَلَّفْتُ لَكَ الْجَيْشَ is "I made the army swear (the oath) to you", the oath of allegiance to an heir.

sentences.t: فَأَطْرَقَ شَرْكَانُ بِرَأْسِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: fa-aṭraqa Sharkānu bi-raʾsihi ilā al-arḍi
sentences.l: And Sharkān bowed with his head to the earth.
sentences.i: Sharkān bowed his head to the ground.
sentences.n: The sentence goes on in the next unit. أَطْرَقَ is to lower the head or gaze, in thought or dismay.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَحَى أَنْ يُكَافِحَ وَالِدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-istaḥā an yukāfiḥa wālidahu
sentences.l: And he was-ashamed that he confront his father,
sentences.i: He was ashamed to confront his father face to face,
sentences.n: يُكَافِحَ is "to meet face to face, to confront". This clause may be the tail of a sentence begun in the previous unit.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَبِلَ الْخَرَزَةَ وَقَامَ وَهُوَ لَايَعْلَمُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْغَيْظِ
sentences.tr: thumma qabila al-kharazata wa-qāma wa-huwa lā-yaʿlamu kayfa yaṣnaʿu min shiddati al-ghayẓi
sentences.l: Then he accepted the bead and arose, and he not-knowing how he should do, from the intensity of the rage.
sentences.i: Then he took the bead and rose, not knowing what to do, so fierce was his rage.
sentences.n: لَايَعْلَمُ (lā yaʿlamu) is printed as one word, with no space; we keep it glued.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ مَاشِيًا حَتَّى دَخَلَ قَصْرَ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla māshiyan ḥattā dakhala qaṣra al-malikati Abrīzata
sentences.l: And he did not cease walking until he entered the palace of the queen Abrīza.
sentences.i: He walked on without stopping until he entered the palace of Queen Abrīza.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهَا قَامَتْ قَائِمَةً لَهُ وَشَكَرَتْهُ عَلَى فِعَالِهِ وَدَعَتْ لَهُ وَأَوَالِدِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbala ʿalayhā qāmat qāʾimatan lahu wa-shakaratahu ʿalā fiʿālihi wa-daʿat lahu wa-awālidihi
sentences.l: And when he turned toward her, she rose, standing, for him, and thanked him for his deeds, and prayed for him and his awālid [sic].
sentences.i: When he came to her, she rose and stood before him, thanked him for what he had done, and prayed for him and for his sons.
sentences.n: وَاوَالِدِهِ is printed with the alif and lām transposed: the sense wants وَأَوْلَادِهِ, "and his sons" (or perhaps وَوَالِدِهِ, "and his father"). We point the letters as printed (awālidihi) and translate by sense. قَامَتْ قَائِمَةً, "rose, standing", is a stock phrase for rising in respect.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسَتْ وَأَجْلَسَتْهُ فِي جَانِبِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-jalasat wa-ajlasathu fī jānibihā
sentences.l: And she sat and made-him-sit at her side.
sentences.i: She sat and seated him beside her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَقَرَّ بِهِ الْجُلُوسُ رَأَتْ فِي وَجْهِهِ الْغَيْظَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istaqarra bihi al-julūsu raʾat fī wajhihi al-ghayẓa
sentences.l: And when the sitting settled with him, she saw in his face the rage,
sentences.i: When he had settled in his seat, she saw anger in his face,

sentences.t: فَسَأَلَتْهُ فَأَخْبَرَهَا أَنَّ وَالِدَهُ رُزِقَ مِنْ صَفِيَّةَ وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا وَأُنْثَى
sentences.tr: fa-saʾalathu fa-akhbarahā anna wālidahu ruziqa min Ṣafiyyata waladan dhakaran wa-unthā
sentences.l: and she asked him, and he informed her that his father was provided, from Ṣafiyya, a child, male, and a female.
sentences.i: and she asked him; and he told her that his father had been blessed by Ṣafiyya with a boy and a girl.
sentences.n: رُزِقَ مِنْ is "was granted (children) by"; the verb is the one used of God's providing. وَأُنْثَى is the indefinite "a female", set beside وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا, "a male child".

sentences.t: وَسَمَّى الْوَلَدَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَالْأُنْثَى نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-sammā al-walada Ḍawʾa al-Makāni wa-al-unthā Nuzhata al-Zamāni
sentences.l: And he named the boy Light-of-the-Place and the female Delight-of-the-Age.
sentences.i: He named the boy Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the girl Nuzhat al-Zamān.
sentences.n: The names mean "Light of the Place" and "Delight of the Age".

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا إِنَّهُ أَعْطَاهُمَا خَرَزَتَيْنِ وَدَفَعَ لِي وَاحِدَةً فَتَرَكْتُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā innahu aʿṭāhumā kharazatayni wa-dafaʿa lī wāḥidatan fa-taraktuhā
sentences.l: And he said to her that he gave the two of them two beads, and handed to me one, and I left it.
sentences.i: He told her that his father had given the two children two beads and had handed one to him, and he had left it aside.
sentences.n: The report slips from the third person into Sharkān's own first person at دَفَعَ لِي, "handed to me", and فَتَرَكْتُهَا, "and I left it"; the idiomatic line smooths the shift. Two beads for the infants and one for Sharkān make the three beads of the queen's reply below.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا إِلَى الْآنَ لَمْ أَعْلَمْ بِذَلِكَ إِلَّافِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā ilā al-āna lam aʿlam bi-dhālika illā fī hādhā al-waqti
sentences.l: And I, up to now, had not known of that except at this time,
sentences.i: I knew nothing of it until this very hour,
sentences.n: إِلَّافِي is printed as one word, إلا and في run together; we keep it glued.

sentences.t: وَالْحَالُ أَنَّ لَهُمَا سِتَّةُ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ḥālu anna lahumā sittatu sinīna
sentences.l: and the state is that to the two of them are six years.
sentences.i: though they are already six years old.
sentences.n: سِتَّةُ سِنِينَ, with the feminine-looking ستة before a plural, is not Classical (which wants ست سنين); we point it as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِمْتُ ذَلِكَ أَخَذَنِي الْغَيْظُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿalimtu dhālika akhadhanī al-ghayẓu
sentences.l: And when I knew that, the rage took me,
sentences.i: When I learned of it, anger seized me.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَخْبَرْتُكِ بِسَبَبِ غَيْظِي وَلَمْ أُخْفِ عَنْكِ شَيْئًا
sentences.tr: wa-qad akhbartuki bi-sababi ghayẓī wa-lam ukhfi ʿanki shayʾan
sentences.l: and I have informed you of the cause of my rage, and I did not hide from you a thing.
sentences.i: I have told you the cause of my anger and kept nothing from you.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا الْآنَ خَائِفٌ عَلَيْكِ أَنْ يَتَزَوَّجَ بِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā al-āna khāʾifun ʿalayki an yatazawwaja bi-ki
sentences.l: And I am now afraid for you that he marry with you,
sentences.i: And now I fear for you, that he will marry you.
sentences.n: يَتَزَوَّجَ بِكِ, with بِـ, is the common Middle Arabic way of saying "marry her"; Classical takes the woman as direct object.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ قَدْأَ حَبَّكِ وَرَأَيْتُ مِنْهُ عَلَامَةَ الطَّمَعِ فِيكِ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu qadʾa ḥabbaki wa-raʾaytu minhu ʿalāmata al-ṭamaʿi fīki
sentences.l: for indeed he has loved you, and I saw from him the sign of covetousness in you.
sentences.i: for he has fallen in love with you, and I have seen in him the mark of his longing for you.
sentences.n: The print runs the alif of أَحَبَّكِ onto the previous word and writes قدا حبك; we follow the printed division, pointing it as قَدْ أَحَبَّكِ, "he has loved you".

sentences.t: فَمَا تَقُولِينَ إِذَا أَرَادَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-mā taqūlīna idhā arāda dhālika
sentences.l: So what do you say if he wants that?
sentences.i: What will you say if he wishes it?

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ اعْلَمْ يَا شَرْكَانُ أَنَّ أَبَاكَ مَالَهُ حُكْمٌ عَلَيَّ وَلَا يَقْدِرُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَنِي بِغَيْرِ رِضَائِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālati iʿlam yā Sharkānu anna abāka mālahu ḥukmun ʿalayya wa-lā yaqdiru an yaʾkhudhanī bi-ghayri riḍāʾī
sentences.l: And she said: Know, O Sharkān, that your father, to-him no rule over me, and he is not able to take me without my consent;
sentences.i: She said, "Know, Sharkān, that your father has no authority over me, and he cannot take me without my consent.
sentences.n: مَالَهُ is printed as one word (mā la-hu, "he has not"). The shadda on عَلَيَّ is printed in the edition and kept.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ كَانَ يَأْخُذُنِي غَصْبًا قَتَلْتُ نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: wa-in kāna yaʾkhudhunī ghaṣban qataltu nafsī
sentences.l: and if he is taking me by force, I have killed myself.
sentences.i: And if he takes me by force, I shall kill myself.
sentences.n: The perfect قَتَلْتُ, "I have killed", stands for a firm resolve in the apodosis.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا ثَلَٰثُ خَرَزَاتٍ فَمَا كَانَ عَلَى بَالِي أَنْ يُنْعِمَ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَوْلَادِهِ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā thalāthu kharazātin fa-mā kāna ʿalā bālī an yunʿima ʿalā aḥadin min awlādihi bi-shayʾin minhā
sentences.l: And as for three beads, it was not upon my mind that he would show-favour upon one of his children with a thing of them,
sentences.i: As for the three beads, it never crossed my mind that he would bestow any of them upon any of his sons,
sentences.n: ثلث is the defective spelling of ثلاث, "three", and takes the dagger alif. ما كان على بالي is "it was not on my mind".

sentences.t: وَمَا طَنَنْتُ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ يَجْعَلُهَا فِي خَزَائِنِهِ مَعَ ذَخَائِرِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā ṭanantu illā annahu yajʿaluhā fī khazāʾinihi maʿa dhakhāʾirihi
sentences.l: and I did not suppose except that he would put them in his treasuries with his stores.
sentences.i: for I supposed only that he would lay them away in his treasuries with his other hoards.
sentences.n: طَنَنْتُ is printed with ط; the verb is ظَنَنْتُ, "I supposed", and the print has the wrong letter. We point the letters as printed.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ أَشْتَهِي مِنْ إِحْسَانِكَ أَنْ تَهَبَنِي الْخَرَزَةَ الَّتِي أَعْطَاهَا لَكَ وَالِدُكَ إِنْ قَبِلْتَهَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin ashtahī min iḥsānika an tahabanī al-kharazata allatī aʿṭāhā laka wāliduka in qabiltahā minhu
sentences.l: But I desire, of your kindness, that you give me the bead which your father gave to you, if you accepted it from him.
sentences.i: But I would ask it of your kindness that you give me the bead your father gave you, if you took it from him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And he said to her: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: He said to her, "With hearing and obedience."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَعْطَاهَا إِيَّاهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu aʿṭāhā iyyāhā
sentences.l: Then he gave her it.
sentences.i: Then he gave it to her.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَا تَخَفْ وَتَحَدَّثَتْ مَعَهُ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu lā takhaf wa-taḥaddathat maʿahu sāʿatan
sentences.l: And she said to him: Do not fear; and she conversed with him an hour,
sentences.i: She said to him, "Do not be afraid," and talked with him for an hour,

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يَسْمَعَ أَبِي أَنِّي عِنْدَكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu innī akhāfu an yasmaʿa abī annī ʿindakum
sentences.l: and she said to him: Indeed I fear that my father hear that I am with you,
sentences.i: and said to him, "I fear that my father will hear that I am with you.

sentences.t: فَمَا يَقْعُدُ عَنِّي وَيَسْعَى فِى طَلَبِي
sentences.tr: fa-mā yaqʿudu ʿannī wa-yasʿā fī ṭalabī
sentences.l: and he will not sit away from me, and will strive in the seeking of me,
sentences.i: He will not sit idle, but will bestir himself to seek me,

sentences.t: وَيَتَّفِقُ هُوَ وَالْمَلِكُ أَفْرِيدُونُ لِأَجْلِ ابْنَتِهِ صَفِيَّةَ فَيَأْتِيَانِ إِلَيْكُمْ بِعَسَاكِرَ وَتَكُونُ ضَجَّةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-yattafiqu huwa wa-al-maliku Afrīdūnu li-ajli ibnatihi Ṣafiyyata fa-yaʾtiyāni ilaykum bi-ʿasākira wa-takūnu ḍajjatun ʿaẓīmatun
sentences.l: and he will agree, he and the king Afrīdūn, for the sake of his daughter Ṣafiyya, and the two will come to you with armies, and there will be a great clamour.
sentences.i: and he and King Afrīdūn will join together for the sake of his daughter Ṣafiyya, and the two of them will come against you with armies, and there will be a great uproar."
sentences.n: فَيَأْتِيَانِ إِلَيْكُمْ بِعَسَاكِرَ is "they will come to you with armies"; أَتَى بِـ is "to come with, bring".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ ذَلِكَ قَالَ لَهَا يَا مَوْلَاتِي إِذَا كُنْتِ رَاضِيَةً بِالْإِقَامَةِ عِنْدَنَا لَاتُفَكِّرِي فِيهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Sharkānu dhālika qāla lahā yā mawlātī idhā kunti rāḍiyatan bi-al-iqāmati ʿindanā lā-tufakkirī fīhim
sentences.l: And when Sharkān heard that, he said to her: O my mistress, if you are content with the staying with us, do not think about them,
sentences.i: When Sharkān heard that, he said to her, "My lady, if you are content to stay with us, give them no thought,
sentences.n: لَاتُفَكِّرِي is printed as one word, and is kept glued.

sentences.t: وَلَوْ يَجْتَمِعُ عَلَيْنَا كُلُّ مَنْ فِى الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-law yajtamiʿu ʿalaynā kullu man fī al-barri wa-al-baḥri
sentences.l: even if there gather against us all who are in the land and the sea.
sentences.i: even if everyone on land and sea should gather against us."
sentences.n: وَلَوْ يَجْتَمِعُ puts an imperfect after لَوْ, where Classical Arabic uses the perfect; it is the Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَا يَكُونُ إِلَّا الْخَيْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu mā yakūnu illā al-khayru
sentences.l: And she said to him: There will be nothing but the good.
sentences.i: She said to him, "Nothing but good will come of it.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنْتُمْ إِنْ أَحْسَنْتُمْ إِلَيَّ قَعَدْتُ عِنْدَكُمْ وَإِنْ أَسَأْنُمْ إِلَيَّ رَحَلْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-hā antum in aḥsantum ilayya qaʿadtu ʿindakum wa-in asaʾnum ilayya raḥaltu min ʿindikum
sentences.l: And here are you: if you do-well to me, I have sat with you, and if you do-ill to me, I have departed from your presence.
sentences.i: Here you are: if you treat me well, I shall stay with you, and if you wrong me, I shall depart from you."
sentences.n: أَسَأْنُمْ is printed with ن where the sense wants ت (أَسَأْتُمْ, "you did ill"); we point the letters as printed. The shadda on إِلَيَّ is printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَمَرَتِ الْجَوَارِيَ بِإِحْضَارِ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْأَكْلِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā amarati al-jawāriya bi-iḥḍāri shayʾin mina al-akli
sentences.l: Then that she commanded the girls with the bringing of a thing of the eating,
sentences.i: Then she bade her maids bring something to eat,

sentences.t: فَقُدِّمَتِ الْمَائِدَةُ فَأَكَلَ شَرْكَانُ شَيْئًا يَسِيرًا وَمَضَى إِلَى دَارِهِ مَهْمُومًا مَغْمُومًا
sentences.tr: fa-quddimati al-māʾidatu fa-akala Sharkānu shayʾan yasīran wa-maḍā ilā dārihi mahmūman maghmūman
sentences.l: and the table was presented, and Sharkān ate a thing, little, and went to his house, worried, grieved.
sentences.i: and the table was set, and Sharkān ate a little, then went home troubled and grieved.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amrihi
sentences.l: This is what was of his affair.
sentences.i: So much for what befell him.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ وَالِدِهِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ فَإِنَّهُ بَعْدَ انْصِرَافِ وَلَدِهِ شَرْكَانَ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ قَامَ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى جَارِيَتِهِ صَفِيَّةَ وَمَعَهُ تِلْكَ الْخَرَزَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri wālidihi ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni fa-innahu baʿda inṣirāfi waladihi Sharkāna min ʿindihi qāma wa-dakhala ʿalā jāriyatihi Ṣafiyyata wa-maʿahu tilka al-kharazatayni
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of his father ʿUmar son-of-al-Nuʿmān, indeed after the departure of his son Sharkān from his presence, he arose and entered upon his girl Ṣafiyya, and with him those two-beads.
sentences.i: As for his father, ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, once his son Sharkān had left him, he rose and went in to his slave girl Ṣafiyya, with the two beads in his hand.
sentences.n: تِلْكَ الْخَرَزَتَيْنِ uses the singular تلك with a dual noun, and the oblique dual after a nominative-style clause; both are Middle Arabic. دَخَلَ عَلَى is "to go in to, visit".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ نَهَضَتْ قَائِمَهْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهَا إِلَى أَنْ جَلَسَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾathu nahaḍat qāʾimah ʿalā qadamayhā ilā an jalasa
sentences.l: And when she saw him, she rose, standing, upon her two feet, until he sat.
sentences.i: When she saw him she rose to her feet and stood until he had sat down.
sentences.n: قَائِمَهْ is printed with final ه where the feminine ending ة is meant; we point the printed letter with a pausal sukūn.

sentences.t: فَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ أَوْلَادُهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَنُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-aqbala ʿalayhi awlāduhu Ḍawʾu al-Makāni wa-Nuzhatu al-Zamāni
sentences.l: And there turned toward him his children, Light-of-the-Place and Delight-of-the-Age.
sentences.i: Then his children, Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Nuzhat al-Zamān, came up to him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَهُمَا قَبَّلَهُمَا وَعَلَّقَ عَلَى كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا خَرَزَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾahumā qabbalahumā wa-ʿallaqa ʿalā kulli wāḥidin minhumā kharazatan
sentences.l: And when he saw the two of them, he kissed them, and hung upon each one of them a bead.
sentences.i: When he saw them he kissed them, and hung a bead upon each of them,

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَا بِهِمَا وَقَبَّلَا يَدَيْهِ وَأَقْبَلَا عَلَى أُمِّهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥā bihimā wa-qabbalā yadayhi wa-aqbalā ʿalā ummihimā
sentences.l: And the two rejoiced in the two, and kissed his hands, and turned toward their mother,
sentences.i: and they were delighted with them, kissed his hands, and turned to their mother,

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَتْ بِهِمَا وَدَعَتْ لِلْمَلِكِ بِطُولِ الدَّوَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥat bihimā wa-daʿat li-al-maliki bi-ṭūli al-dawāmi
sentences.l: and she rejoiced in the two, and prayed for the king with length of continuance.
sentences.i: and she too rejoiced in them, and prayed that the king might endure long.
sentences.n: طُولِ الدَّوَامِ, "length of continuance", is a stock wish for long life.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الْمَلِكُ وَأَنْتِ هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةَ كُلَّهَا لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ لَمْ تُعْلِمِينِي أَنَّكِ ابْنَةُ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-maliku wa-anti hādhihi al-muddata kullahā li-ayyi shayʾin lam tuʿlimīnī annaki ibnatu al-maliki Afrīdūna maliki al-Quṣṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: And the king said to her: And you, this whole period, for what thing did you not inform me that you are the daughter of the king Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople,
sentences.i: The king said to her, "All this time, why did you not tell me that you are the daughter of King Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople,

sentences.t: لِأَجْلِ أَنْ أَزِيدَ فِي إِكْرَامِكِ وَأُوَسِّعَ لَكِ وَأَرْفَعَ مَنْزِلَتَكِ
sentences.tr: li-ajli an azīda fī ikrāmiki wa-uwassiʿa laki wa-arfaʿa manzilataki
sentences.l: for the sake that I add in your honouring, and widen for you, and raise your station?
sentences.i: so that I might have honoured you the more, made room for you, and raised your rank?"
sentences.n: The sentence may run on into the next unit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ صَفِيَّةُ ذَلِكَ قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat Ṣafiyyatu dhālika qālat
sentences.l: And when Ṣafiyya heard that, she said:
sentences.i: When Ṣafiyya heard that, she said,

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ وَمَاذَا أُرِيدُ أَكْثَرَ وَأَعْلَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْمَنْزِلَةِ الَّتِي أَنَا فِيهَا وَأَنَا مَغْمُورَةٌ بِإِنْعَامِكَ وَخَيْرِكَ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-maliku wa-mādhā urīdu akthara wa-aʿlā min hādhihi al-manzilati allatī anā fīhā wa-anā maghmūratun bi-inʿāmika wa-khayrika
sentences.l: O king, and what do I want more and higher than this station that I am in it, and I am submerged-one in your bestowal and your goodness,
sentences.i: "O king, what more would I want, or what higher than this station I am in, when I am drowned in your favours and your goodness,
sentences.n: وَأَعْلَا is printed with a plain alif where Classical spelling has ى (أَعْلَى, "higher"); we point the printed letters. مَا ... أُرِيدُ أَكْثَرَ وَأَعْلَا: the two comparatives are accusative objects of "want".

sentences.t: وَقَدْ رَزَقَنِي اللَّهُ مِنْكَ بِوَلَدَيْنِ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى
sentences.tr: wa-qad razaqanī Allāhu minka bi-waladayni dhakarin wa-unthā
sentences.l: and God has indeed provided me, from you, with two children, a male and a female?"
sentences.i: when God has granted me, by you, two children, a boy and a girl?"
sentences.n: رَزَقَ بِـ takes the thing granted with بِـ in this construction ("provide someone with"). ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى is an apposition to the two children: "a male and a female".

sentences.t: فَأَعْجَبَ الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ كَلَامُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-aʿjaba al-malika ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni kalāmuhā
sentences.l: And her speech pleased the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: Her words pleased King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.n: أَعْجَبَ takes the person pleased as its object (accusative) and the pleasing thing as its subject, so الْمَلِكَ is accusative and كَلَامُهَا nominative. The printed بن is pointed بْنَ, with the alif of ابن dropped as usual between a name and its patronymic.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَضَى مِنْ عِنْدِهَا وَأَفْرَدَ لَهَا وَلِأَوْلَادِهَا قَصْرًا عَجِيبًا
sentences.tr: thumma maḍā min ʿindihā wa-afrada lahā wa-li-awlādihā qaṣran ʿajīban
sentences.l: Then he went from her presence, and set apart for her and for her children a palace, wondrous,
sentences.i: Then he left her and set apart for her and her children a wondrous palace,

sentences.t: وَرَتَّبَ لَهُمُ الْخَدَمَ وَالْحَشَمَ وَالْفُقَهَاءَ وَالْحُكَمَاءَ وَالْفَلَكِيَّةَ وَالْأَطِبَّاءَ وَالْجِرَا يْحِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: wa-rattaba lahumu al-khadama wa-al-ḥashama wa-al-fuqahāʾa wa-al-ḥukamāʾa wa-al-falakiyyata wa-al-aṭibbāʾa wa-al-jirā yḥiyyata
sentences.l: and appointed for them the servants, and the retinue, and the jurists, and the sages, and the astronomers, and the physicians, and the surgeons,
sentences.i: and he appointed for them servants and retinue, jurists and sages, astronomers, physicians and surgeons,
sentences.n: The last word is printed in two pieces, الجرا يحية, with a stray ي. The sense is clearly الْجَرَّاحِيَّة, "surgeons" (jarrāḥ, one who cuts wounds), beside the physicians; we point the printed letters by sense and keep the space. الْفَلَكِيَّة are astronomers or astrologers (falak, sphere).

sentences.t: وَأَوْصَاهُمْ بِهِمْ وَزَادَ فِي إِكْرَامِهِمْ وَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِمْ غَايَةَ الْإِحْسَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-awṣāhum bihim wa-zāda fī ikrāmihim wa-aḥsana ilayhim ghāyata al-iḥsāni
sentences.l: and charged them with them, and increased in honouring them, and did good to them to-the-utmost of doing-good.
sentences.i: and he charged them to care for them, and increased his honouring of them, and was generous to them to the utmost.
sentences.n: أَوْصَى بِـ is "to charge (someone) with the care of"; the first هُمْ is the servants, the second the family. غَايَةَ الْإِحْسَانِ is an adverbial accusative: "to the furthest degree of kindness".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى قَصْرِ الْمَمْلَكَةِ وَالْمُحَاكَمَةِ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: thumma rajaʿa ilā qaṣri al-mamlakati wa-al-muḥākamati bayna al-nāsi
sentences.l: Then he returned to the palace of the kingdom and of the adjudication between the people.
sentences.i: Then he went back to the royal palace and to judging between the people.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ لَهُ مَعَ صَفِيَّةَ وَأَوْلَادِهَا
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna lahu maʿa Ṣafiyyata wa-awlādihā
sentences.l: This is what was to him with Ṣafiyya and her children;
sentences.i: So much for what passed between him and Ṣafiyya and her children;
sentences.n: The stock formula هَذَا مَا كَانَ ... وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ ... shifts the story from one party to another: "this is what happened with X; as for what happened with Y ...".

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ مَعَ الْمَلِكَهِ أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amrihi maʿa al-malikahi Abrīzata
sentences.l: and as for what was from his affair with the queen Abrīza,
sentences.i: but as for his dealings with Queen Abrīza,
sentences.n: الْمَلِكَهِ is printed with final ه where the sense wants ة (الْمَلِكَة), the same slip as elsewhere in the print; we point the printed letter and read it as "queen".

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ اشْتَغَلَ بِحُبِّهَا وَصَارَ لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا مَشْغُوفًا بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-malika ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni ishtaghala bi-ḥubbihā wa-ṣāra laylan wa-nahāran mashghūfan bihā
sentences.l: indeed the king ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān busied-himself with love of her, and became, night and day, smitten-to-the-heart with her.
sentences.i: King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān was consumed with love of her, and night and day he was heartsick for her.
sentences.n: مَشْغُوفٌ is one whose heart (شَغَاف) has been pierced by love. لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا, "by night and by day", are adverbial accusatives.

sentences.t: وَفِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ يَدْخُلُ إِلَيْهَا وَيَتَحَدَّثُ عِنْدَهَا وَيُلَوِّحُ لَهَا بِالْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī kulli laylatin yadkhulu ilayhā wa-yataḥaddathu ʿindahā wa-yulawwiḥu lahā bi-al-kalāmi
sentences.l: And in every night he would enter to her, and converse in her presence, and hint to her with speech,
sentences.i: Every night he went in to her and talked with her, and hinted to her in words of what he wanted,
sentences.n: The present tense after كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ is habitual ("he would"). لَوَّحَ بِـ is "to hint, to allude"; we add "of what he wanted" in the idiomatic line only.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ تَرُدَّ لَهُ جَوَابًا
sentences.tr: fa-lam tarudda lahu jawāban
sentences.l: but she did not return to him an answer;
sentences.i: but she gave him no answer.

sentences.t: بَلْ تَقُولُ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ أَنَا فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ مَالِي غَرَضٌ فِى الرِّجَالِ
sentences.tr: bal taqūlu yā malika al-zamāni anā fī hādhā al-waqti mālī gharaḍun fī al-rijāli
sentences.l: rather she would say: O king of the time, I, at this time, not for me is a purpose in men.
sentences.i: Rather she would say, "O king of the age, at this time I have no desire for men."
sentences.n: مَالِي (printed as one word, mā + lī) غَرَضٌ is the ordinary way to say "I have no (need, wish)": مَا negates a sentence of possession (لِي ... غَرَضٌ, "to me ... a wish"). The print has فى with ى here and في with ي just before.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى تَمَنُّعَهَا مِنْهُ اشْتَدَّ بِهِ الْغَرَامُ وَزَادَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَجْدُ وَالْهَيَامُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā tamannuʿahā minhu ishtadda bihi al-gharāmu wa-zāda ʿalayhi al-wajdu wa-al-hayāmu
sentences.l: And when he saw her refusing-herself from him, the passion grew intense with him, and the ardour and the distraction increased upon him.
sentences.i: When he saw how she held herself from him, his passion grew fierce, and ardour and distraction increased upon him.
sentences.n: الْغَرَامُ, الْوَجْدُ and الْهَيَامُ are near-synonyms for love-passion, ardour and love-madness; the rhyme (-ām) of the first and last makes this a piece of rhymed prose. رَأَى is printed with the hamza on the alif, and we keep it so.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَعْيَاهُ ذَلِكَ أَحْضَرَ وَزِيرَهُ دَنْدَانَ وَأَطْلَعَهُ عَلَى مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ مِنْ مَحَبَّةِ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ ابْنَةِ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ وَأَخْبَرَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aʿyāhu dhālika aḥḍara wazīrahu Dandāna wa-aṭlaʿahu ʿalā mā fī qalbihi min maḥabbati al-malikati Abrīzata ibnati al-maliki Ḥardūba wa-akhbarahu
sentences.l: And when that wearied him, he summoned his vizier Dandān, and made him acquainted with what was in his heart of love of the queen Abrīza, daughter of the king Ḥardūb, and informed him
sentences.i: When this wore him out, he summoned his vizier Dandān and let him know what was in his heart, his love for Queen Abrīza, daughter of King Ḥardūb, and told him
sentences.n: أَعْيَا is "to tire out, leave helpless"; أَطْلَعَهُ عَلَى is "to let him look upon, acquaint him with". The sentence runs on into the next unit, which gives the content of what he told.

sentences.t: أَنَّهَا لَا تَدْخُلُ فِي طَاعَتِهِ وَقَدْ قَتَلَهُ حُبُّهَا وَلَمْ يَنَلْ مِنْهَا شَيْئًا
sentences.tr: annahā lā tadkhulu fī ṭāʿatihi wa-qad qatalahu ḥubbuhā wa-lam yanal minhā shayʾan
sentences.l: that she would not enter into his obedience, and her love had indeed killed him, and he had not obtained from her anything.
sentences.i: that she would not submit to him, that love of her was killing him, and that he had got nothing from her.
sentences.n: دَخَلَ فِي طَاعَةِ فُلَانٍ is "to come under someone's obedience", here said of a woman refusing a man. The pointing شَيْئًا keeps the print's precomposed ئ.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ ذَلِكَ قَالَ لِلْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru Dandānu dhālika qāla li-al-maliki
sentences.l: And when the vizier Dandān heard that, he said to the king:
sentences.i: When the vizier Dandān heard that, he said to the king,

sentences.t: إِذَا جَنَّ اللَّيْلُ فَخُذْ مَعَكَ قِطْعَةَ بَنْجٍ مِقْدَارَ مِثْقَالٍ وَادْخُلْ عَلَيْهَا وَاشْرَبْ مَعَهَا شَيْئًا مِنَ الْخَمْرِ
sentences.tr: idhā janna al-laylu fa-khudh maʿaka qiṭʿata banjin miqdāra mithqālin wa-udkhul ʿalayhā wa-ishrab maʿahā shayʾan mina al-khamri
sentences.l: When the night grows-dark, then take with you a piece of banj, the measure of a mithqāl, and enter upon her, and drink with her something of the wine;
sentences.i: "When night has fallen, take with you a piece of henbane-drug, about a mithqāl in weight, and go in to her and drink a little wine with her.
sentences.n: بَنْج (banj, from Persian) is a narcotic, here a drug that puts a person into a deep sleep; the Nights usually means a henbane or hemp preparation. A مِثْقَال is a small weight, about one dirham and a half or a little more. جَنَّ اللَّيْلُ, "the night covered", is the standard phrase for nightfall.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا كَانَ وَقْتُ الْفَرَاغِ مِنَ الشَّرَابِ وَالْمُنَادَمَةِ فَأَعْطِهَا الْقَدَحَ الْأَخِيرَ وَاجْعَلْ فِيهِ ذَلِكَ الْبَنْجَ وَاسْقِيهِ لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā kāna waqtu al-farāghi mina al-sharābi wa-al-munādamati fa-aʿṭihā al-qadaḥa al-akhīra wa-ijʿal fīhi dhālika al-banja wa-isqīhi lahā
sentences.l: And when it is the time of the finishing from the drinking and the carousing, then give her the last cup, and put in it that banj, and give-it-to-drink to her;
sentences.i: When the time comes to stop the drinking and the carousing, give her the last cup, with the drug put in it, and have her drink it.
sentences.n: وَاسْقِيهِ is printed with a yā' that a Classical imperative would not have (وَاسْقِهِ, "give it to drink"): a lengthened Middle Arabic form, which we point as printed. الْمُنَادَمَة is companionship over wine.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا مَا تَصِلُ إِلَى مَرْقَدِهَا إِلَّاوَقَدْ تَحَكَّمَ عَلَيْهَا الْبَنْجُ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā mā taṣilu ilā marqadihā illā-wa-qad taḥakkama ʿalayhā al-banju
sentences.l: for she will not reach her sleeping-place except that the banj has already taken-control over her;
sentences.i: She will not reach her bed before the drug has taken hold of her.
sentences.n: إِلَّاوَقَدْ is printed as one word, illā + wa-qad; we point it as the two words glued, as the print has no space. إِلَّا وَقَدْ after a negative means "without ... already": the drug will have mastered her by the time she reaches her bed. مَا تَصِلُ uses the present for the future.

sentences.t: فَتَدْخُلُ أَنْتَ عَلَيْهَا وَتَتَّصِلُ بِهَا وَتَبْلُغُ غَرَضَكَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-tadkhulu anta ʿalayhā wa-tattaṣilu bihā wa-tablughu gharaḍaka minhā
sentences.l: then you enter upon her, and join-yourself with her, and attain your purpose from her;
sentences.i: Then you go in to her, lie with her, and have your will of her.
sentences.n: اتَّصَلَ بِـ, "to join with", is here a plain word for sexual union with the sleeping woman; the Arabic does not soften it, and the next lines carry it out. The verbs are present tenses continuing the instruction.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا مَا عِنْدِي مِنَ الرَّأْيِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā mā ʿindī mina al-raʾyi
sentences.l: and this is what is with me of the opinion.
sentences.i: That is the counsel I have to give."
sentences.n: الرَّأْيِ is printed with the hamza on the alif, and we keep it so.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلِكُ نِعْمَ مَا أَشَرْتَ بِهِ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-maliku niʿma mā ashrta bihi ʿalayya
sentences.l: And the king said to him: How excellent is what you have indicated by it upon me!
sentences.i: The king said to him, "What an excellent thing you have advised me!"
sentences.n: عَلَيَّ carries a shadda in the edition, and we keep it. أَشَارَ عَلَى is "to advise". نِعْمَ مَا is "excellent is what ...", the verb of praise with relative مَا.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ عَمَدَ إِلَى خِزَانَتِهِ وَأَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا قِطْعَةَ بَنْجٍ مُكَرَّرٍ لَوْشَمَّهُ الْفِيلُ لَرَقَدَ مِنَ السَّنَةِ إِلَى السَّنَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu ʿamada ilā khizānatihi wa-akhraja minhā qiṭʿata banjin mukarraran law-shammahu al-fīlu la-raqada mina al-sanati ilā al-sanati
sentences.l: Then that he made-for his cabinet, and brought out from it a piece of banj, refined, that if the elephant smelled it, it would sleep from the year to the year.
sentences.i: Then he went to his cabinet and took from it a piece of refined drug so strong that, had an elephant smelled it, it would have slept from one year to the next.
sentences.n: لَوْشَمَّهُ is printed as one word, law + shammahu. مُكَرَّرٍ, "redistilled, refined", is pointed as a genitive agreeing with بَنْجٍ, but the print could also intend the accusative مُكَرَّرًا; we follow the genitive. The elephant is the stock measure of a drug's strength.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلَهَا فِي جَيْبِهِ وَصَبَرَ إِلَى أَنْ مَضَى قَلِيلٌ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ فِي قَصْرِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿalahā fī jaybihi wa-ṣabara ilā an maḍā qalīlun mina al-layli wa-dakhala ʿalā al-malikati Abrīzata fī qaṣrihā
sentences.l: And he put it in his pocket, and waited until a little of the night had passed, and entered upon the queen Abrīza in her palace.
sentences.i: He put it in his pocket and waited until a little of the night had passed, and then went in to Queen Abrīza in her palace.
sentences.n: The sentence runs over the page break (p. 394 to p. 395) between الْمَلِكَةِ and أَبْرِيزَةَ.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ قَامَتْ لَهُ قَائِمَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾathu qāmat lahu qāʾimatan
sentences.l: And when she saw him, she rose for him, standing,
sentences.i: When she saw him she stood up in respect for him,
sentences.n: رَأَتْهُ and قَائِمَةً keep the hamza on the carrier as printed. قَائِمَةً is an accusative of state, "standing" (a pleonastic circumstantial after قَامَتْ).

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ لَهَا بِالْجُلُوسِ فَجَلَسَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-amara lahā bi-al-julūsi fa-jalasat
sentences.l: and he commanded her to sit, and she sat.
sentences.i: and he bade her sit, and she sat.
sentences.n: أَمَرَ لَهَا بِالْجُلُوسِ: with لِـ for the person and بِـ for the thing commanded.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسَ عِنْدَهَا وَصَارَ يَتَحَدَّثُ مَعَهَا فِي أَمْرِ الشَّرَابِ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasa ʿindahā wa-ṣāra yataḥaddathu maʿahā fī amri al-sharābi
sentences.l: And he sat with her, and became conversing with her about the matter of the drink,
sentences.i: He sat down beside her and fell to talking with her about the drinking.
sentences.n: This unit opens mid-scene: the king (ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān) is alone with Queen Abrīza, and the wine is about to be served.

sentences.t: فَقَدَّمَتْ سُفْرَةَ الشَّرَابِ وَصَفَّتْ لَهُ الْأَوَانِيَ وَأَوْقَدَتِ الشُّمُوعَ وَأَمَرَتْ بِإِحْضَارِ النَّقْلِ وَالْحَلَاوَاتِ وَالْفَاكِهَةِ وَكُلِّ مَا يَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qaddamat sufrata al-sharābi wa-ṣaffat lahu al-awāniya wa-awqadat al-shumūʿa wa-amarat bi-iḥḍāri al-naqli wa-al-ḥalāwāti wa-al-fākihati wa-kulli mā yaḥtājūna ilayhi
sentences.l: And she presented the spread of the drink, and lined up for him the vessels, and kindled the candles, and commanded the bringing of the nibbles and the sweetmeats and the fruit and all that they need to it,
sentences.i: She laid the drinking-cloth, set out the vessels for him, lit the candles, and ordered the nuts, the sweetmeats, the fruit, and everything else they could need to be brought.
sentences.n: سُفْرَة is the round leather or cloth spread on which food and drink are set out. النَّقْل is the nibbles served with wine (nuts, dried fruit). The shadda on صَفَّتْ is printed in the edition. أَمَرَ بِـ takes the thing commanded with بِـ.

sentences.t: وَصَارَا يَشْرَبَانِ وَالْمَلِكُ يُنَادِمُهَا إِلَى أَنْ دَبَّ السُّكْرُ فِي رَأْسِ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārā yashrabāni wa-al-maliku yunādimuhā ilā an dabba al-sukru fī raʾsi al-malikati Abrīzata
sentences.l: And the two became drinking, the king companioning-her-in-wine, until intoxication crept into the head of the queen Abrīza.
sentences.i: The two of them went on drinking, the king keeping her company over the cups, until the wine crept into Queen Abrīza's head.
sentences.n: دَبَّ السُّكْرُ, "intoxication crept", is a stock phrase for wine taking hold. The shadda on دَبَّ is printed. The أ of رَأْسِ is printed by the edition and stays precomposed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِمَ الْمَلِكُ ذَلِكَ أَخْرَجَ قِطْعَةَ الْبَنْجِ مِنْ جَيْبِهِ وَجَعَلَهَا بَيْنَ أَصَابِعِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿalima al-maliku dhālika akhraja qiṭʿata al-banji min jaybihi wa-jaʿalahā bayna aṣābiʿihi
sentences.l: And when the king knew that, he brought out the piece of banj from his pocket and put it between his fingers,
sentences.i: When the king saw that, he took the piece of the drug from his pocket and held it between his fingers,
sentences.n: الْبَنْج (banj) is the narcotic, here a drug in solid form, that the king has brought to knock the queen unconscious; in the Nights it is typically henbane or hashish.

sentences.t: وَمَلَاً كَأْسًابِيَدِهِ وَشَرِبَهُ وَمَلَأَهُ ثَانِيًا
sentences.tr: wa-malaʾan kaʾsan-bi-yadihi wa-sharibahu wa-malaʾahu thāniyan
sentences.l: and filled a cup with his hand, and drank it, and filled it a second time,
sentences.i: filled a cup with his own hand and drank it off, then filled it a second time,
sentences.n: The print runs كاسا and بيده together ("a cup" + "with his hand"), and puts a tanwin mark on the alif of ملا, where it belongs on the following noun; we keep the printed mark in place and read the verb as مَلَأَ, "he filled". The edition writes كاس for كأس, "cup"; the hamza is ours. شَرِبَهُ is the verb with its regular short vowels, "he drank it".

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِلْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَه اُمْسُكْ وَأَسْقَطَ قِطْعَةَ الْبَنْجِ فِى الْكَأْسِ وَهِيَ لَا تَشْعُرُ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-al-malikati Abrīzah umsuk wa-asqaṭa qiṭʿata al-banji fī al-kaʾsi wa-hiya lā tashʿuru bi-dhālika
sentences.l: and said to the queen Abrīza: Hold! and dropped the piece of banj into the cup, while she does not perceive it of that,
sentences.i: and said to Queen Abrīza, "Hold this," and while she suspected nothing he dropped the piece of the drug into the cup.
sentences.n: The name is printed ابريزه with a final hāʾ (a Middle Arabic spelling of the tāʾ marbūṭa), kept as printed. The printed damma on the alif of اُمسك gives the Form I imperative اُمْسُكْ, "hold, take hold". The object of the command is left out: "hold [the cup]". تَشْعُرُ بِ is "to be aware of", the verb choosing the preposition.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْهُ الْمَلِكَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ وَشَرِبَتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadathu al-malikatu Abrīzatu wa-sharibathu
sentences.l: And the queen Abrīza took it and drank it.
sentences.i: Queen Abrīza took it and drank it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ دُونَ سَاعَةٍ عَلِمَ أَنَّ الْبَنْجَ قَدْ تَحَكَّمَ مَعَهَا وَسَلَبَ إِدْرَاكَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna dūna sāʿatin ʿalima anna al-banja qad taḥakkama maʿahā wa-salaba idrākahā
sentences.l: And when it was less-than an hour, he knew that the banj had taken-hold with her and had stripped her perception.
sentences.i: Within the hour he knew that the drug had taken hold of her and robbed her of her senses.
sentences.n: دُونَ سَاعَةٍ, "short of an hour", means "in less than an hour". تَحَكَّمَ is "to take control"; the sense is that the drug has mastered her.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهَا فَوَجَدَهَا مُلْقَاةً عَلَى ظَهْرِهَا وَقَدْ كَانَتْ قَلَعَتِ السَّرَاوِيلَ مِنْ رِجْلَيْهَا وَرَفَعَ الْهَوَاءُ ذَيْلَ قَمِيصِهَا عَنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma ilayhā fa-wajadahā mulqātan ʿalā ẓahrihā wa-qad kānat qalaʿati al-sarāwīla min rijlayhā wa-rafaʿa al-hawāʾu dhayla qamīṣihā ʿanhā
sentences.l: And he rose to her and found her thrown on her back, she having taken off the trousers from her two legs, and the air had lifted the hem of her shirt from her.
sentences.i: He got up and went to her and found her lying on her back; she had taken the drawers off her legs, and the air had lifted the hem of her shirt away from her.
sentences.n: Note the word order in the last clause: the verb رَفَعَ comes first, then its subject الْهَوَاءُ ("the air"), then the object. The queen took off her drawers before the drug took hold, as a woman does when she is drinking and getting ready for the night.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا الْمَلِكُ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ وَوَجَدَ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهَا شَمْعَةً وَعِنْدَ رِجْلَيْهَا شَمْعَةً تُضِيءُ عَلَى مَابَيْنَ فَخِذَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā al-maliku ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati wa-wajada ʿinda raʾsihā shamʿatan wa-ʿinda rijlayhā shamʿatan tuḍīʾu ʿalā mā bayna fakhidhayhā
sentences.l: And when the king saw her on that state, and found at her head a candle and at her two legs a candle, shining on what is between her two thighs,
sentences.i: When the king saw her in that state, with a candle at her head and a candle at her feet, shining on what lay between her thighs,
sentences.n: The edition prints مابين as one word. Both the precomposed آ of رَآهَا and the precomposed ء of تُضِيءُ are printed, and stay. The candle "shining on" her thighs is the circumstantial clause that explains why he loses control.

sentences.t: حِيلَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ عَقْلِهِ وَوَسْوَسَ لَهُ الشَّيْطَانُ
sentences.tr: ḥīla baynahu wa-bayna ʿaqlihi wa-waswasa lahu al-shayṭānu
sentences.l: it was come-between between him and his mind, and Satan whispered to him,
sentences.i: he was cut off from his reason, and Satan whispered to him.
sentences.n: حِيلَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ عَقْلِهِ is a passive ("it was intervened between him and his mind"): his reason was put out of reach. This is the apodosis of the فَلَمَّا clause before it.

sentences.t: فَمَا تَمَالَكَ نَفْسَهُ حَتَّى قَلَعَ سَرَاوِيلَهُ وَوَقَعَ عَلَيْهَا فَأَزَالَ بَكَارَتَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-mā tamālaka nafsahu ḥattā qalaʿa sarāwīlahu wa-waqaʿa ʿalayhā fa-azāla bakāratahā
sentences.l: And he did not hold himself until he took off his trousers and fell upon her, and removed her virginity.
sentences.i: He could not hold himself back: he pulled off his drawers, lay down on her, and took her virginity.
sentences.n: وَقَعَ عَلَى, "fell upon", is the plain euphemism for taking a woman sexually. The queen is drugged and unconscious: the text presents this as rape and does not say otherwise.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ مِنْ فَوْقِهَا وَدَخَلَ إِلَى جَارِيَةٍ مِنْ جَوَارِيهَا يُقَالُ لَهَا مَرْجَانَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma min fawqihā wa-dakhala ilā jāriyatin min jawārīhā yuqālu lahā Marjānatu
sentences.l: And he rose from above her, and went in to a girl of her girls, it is said to her Marjāna,
sentences.i: Then he rose from her and went to one of her maids, called Marjāna,

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا ادْخُلِي عَلَى سَيِّدَتِكِ كَلِّمِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā udkhulī ʿalā sayyidatiki kallimīhā
sentences.l: and said to her: Go in upon your mistress, speak to her.
sentences.i: and said to her, "Go in to your mistress and speak to her."
sentences.n: He sends the maid in so that she will find her mistress, and tidy her, without suspecting him.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ عَلَى سِتِّهَا فَوَجَدَتْ دَمَهَا يَجْرِي عَلَى سِيقَانِهَا وَهِيَ مُلْقَاةٌ عَلَى ظَهْرِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalati al-jāriyatu ʿalā sittihā fa-wajadat damahā yajrī ʿalā sīqānihā wa-hiya mulqātun ʿalā ẓahrihā
sentences.l: And the girl went in upon her lady, and found her blood running upon her legs, she thrown on her back,
sentences.i: The maid went in to her lady and found her blood running down her legs as she lay on her back.
sentences.n: سِتّ is the colloquial shortening of سَيِّدَة, "lady, mistress" (the Middle Arabic form that gives Cairene sitt); the text moves from سَيِّدَتِكِ in the king's speech to سِتِّهَا in the narration. سِيقَان is a plural of سَاق, "leg, shank".

sentences.t: فَمَدَّتْ يَدَهَا إِلَى مِنْدِيلٍ مِنْ مَنَادِيلِهَا وَأَصْلَحَتْ بِهِ شَأْنَ سَيِّدَتِهَا وَمَسَحَتْ عَنْهَا الدَّمَ وَبَاتَتْ عِنْدَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-maddat yadahā ilā mindīlin min manādīlihā wa-aṣlaḥat bihi shaʾna sayyidatihā wa-masaḥat ʿanhā al-dama wa-bātat ʿindahā
sentences.l: And she stretched her hand to a kerchief of her kerchiefs, and set-right with it the matter of her mistress, and wiped from her the blood, and spent-the-night with her.
sentences.i: She reached out her hand for one of her handkerchiefs, put her mistress to rights with it, wiped the blood from her, and stayed the night beside her.
sentences.n: أَصْلَحَ شَأْنَ means "to put someone's state in order", here tidying her. بَاتَ is "to spend the night" and does not imply sleeping.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ اللهُ تَعَالَى بِالصَّبَاحِ تَقَدَّمَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ مَرْجَانَةُ وَغَسَلَتْ وَجْهَ سَيِّدَتِهَا وَيَدَيْهَا وَرِجْلَيْهَا ثُمَّ جَاءَتْ بِمَاءِ الْوَرْدِ وَغَسَلَتْ بِهِ وَجْهَهَا وَفَمَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa Allāhu taʿālā bi-al-ṣabāḥi taqaddamati al-jāriyatu Marjānatu wa-ghasalat wajha sayyidatihā wa-yadayhā wa-rijlayhā thumma jāʾat bi-māʾi al-wardi wa-ghasalat bihi wajhahā wa-fahā
sentences.l: And when God, exalted, brought-to-morning with the morning, the girl Marjāna came forward and washed the face of her mistress and her two hands and her two feet; then she came with water of the rose and washed with it her face and her mouth,
sentences.i: When God, the Most High, brought the morning, the maid Marjāna came forward and washed her mistress's face, hands, and feet. Then she brought rose-water and washed her face and mouth with it.
sentences.n: أَصْبَحَ اللهُ تَعَالَى بِالصَّبَاحِ is a formula of the narration: "God brought on the morning with the morning", the verb taking its subject (God) and a cognate بِـ phrase. The word فَمَهَا, "her mouth", is the accusative of فَم, "mouth", with the pronoun, where the final م returns (not فَاهَا). The precomposed ء in جَاءَتْ is printed.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ عَطَسَتِ الْمَلِكَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ وَتَثَاوَبَتْ وَتَقَايَتْ ذَلِكَ الْبَنْجَ فَنَزَلَتْ قِطْعَةُ الْبَنْجِ مِنْ بَاطِنِهَا كَالْقُرْصِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ʿaṭasati al-malikatu Abrīzatu wa-tathāwabat wa-taqāyat dhālika al-banja fa-nazalat qiṭʿatu al-banji min bāṭinihā ka-al-qurṣi
sentences.l: And at that the queen Abrīza sneezed and yawned and vomited that banj, and the piece of the banj came down from her inside, like the disc.
sentences.i: At that Queen Abrīza sneezed and yawned and brought up the drug, and the piece of it came out of her belly like a little round cake.
sentences.n: وَتَقَايَتْ is printed without the hamza; the verb is تَقَايَأَتْ (Form VI of قَيَّأَ, "to vomit"), "she vomited". We point the printed letters and note that the final hamza is not written. كَالْقُرْصِ: كَـ, "like", + الْقُرْص, "the disc, round loaf". The piece "came down from her inside" although she vomited it; the text is not exact about where it came from.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنَّهَا غَسَلَتْ فَمَهَا وَيَدَيْهَا وَقَالَتْ لِمَرْجَانَةَ أَعْلِمِينِي بِمَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِي
sentences.tr: thumma annahā ghasalat famahā wa-yadayhā wa-qālat li-Marjānata aʿlimīnī bi-mā kāna min amrī
sentences.l: Then that she washed her mouth and her two hands, and said to Marjāna: Make-me-know with what was of my matter.
sentences.i: Then she washed her mouth and her hands and said to Marjāna, "Tell me what has happened to me."
sentences.n: ثُمَّ أَنَّهَا is the Middle Arabic narrative "then that she", a conjunction that only introduces the next event. أَعْلِمْ بِـ takes the matter told with بِـ.

sentences.t: فَأَعَادَتْ عَلَيْهَا ذَلِكَ وَمَا كَانَ أَمْرُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-aʿādat ʿalayhā dhālika wa-mā kāna amruhā
sentences.l: And she repeated to her that, and what her matter had been,
sentences.i: She told her all of it again and what had befallen her,
sentences.n: أَعَادَ عَلَى, "to repeat to", and the sentence is continued in the next page of the print.

sentences.t: فَعَرَفَتْ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ قَدْ وَقَعَ بِهَا وَوَاصَلَهَا وَتَمَّتْ حِيلَنُهُ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿarafat anna al-malika ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni qad waqaʿa bihā wa-wāṣalahā wa-tammat ḥīlanuhu ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And she knew that the king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān had fallen with her and joined her, and his ruse upon her had been completed,
sentences.i: and she understood that King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān had lain with her and that his trick on her had succeeded.
sentences.n: وَقَعَ بِ is "to fall upon, have to do with" (a woman), with بِـ here instead of the عَلَى used above. وَاصَلَ, "to join", is a euphemism for sexual union.
