The edition prints حيلنه with ن where the sense needs ت: it is a misprint for حِيلَتُهُ, "his ruse"; we point the printed letters.

sentences.t: فَاغْتَمَّتْ لِذَلِكَ غَمًّا شَدِيدًا وَحَجَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ightammat li-dhālika ghamman shadīdan wa-ḥajabat nafsahā
sentences.l: And she grieved for that with a severe grief, and veiled herself,
sentences.i: She was bitterly grieved at this, and shut herself away.
sentences.n: غَمًّا شَدِيدًا is a cognate accusative ("grieved a severe grief"); the shadda on فَاغْتَمَّتْ is printed.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِجَوَارِيهَا امْنَعُوا كُلَّ مَنْ أَرَادَأَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيَّ وَقُولُوا لَهُ أَنَّهَا ضَعِيفَةٌ حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ اللهُ بِي
sentences.tr: wa-qālat li-jawārīhā imnaʿū kulla man arāda an yadkhula ʿalayya wa-qūlū lahu annahā ḍaʿīfatun ḥattā anẓura mādhā yafʿalu Allāhu bī
sentences.l: and said to her girls: Prevent every one who wants to enter upon me, and say to him: that she is weak, until I see what God does with me.
sentences.i: She said to her maids, "Keep out anyone who wishes to come in to me, and tell him that I am unwell, until I see what God will do with me."
sentences.n: ارادان is printed as one word: أَرَادَ and أَنْ run together. The speaker says "say that she is weak", the third person for the report she wants them to give.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ وَصَلَ الْخَبَرُ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِبَرَةَ ضَعِيفَةٌ فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهَا الْأَشْرِبَةَ وَالسُّكَّرَ وَالْمَعَاجِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika waṣala al-khabaru ilā al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni anna al-malikata Abrībarata ḍaʿīfatun fa-arsala ilayhā al-ashribata wa-al-sukkara wa-al-maʿājīna
sentences.l: And at that the news reached the king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān that the queen Abrībara is weak, and he sent to her the drinks and the sugar and the electuaries,
sentences.i: Then word reached King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān that Queen Abrīza was unwell, and he sent her cordials, sugar, and electuaries.
sentences.n: The name is misprinted ابربرة for ابريزة (the yā and zāy are replaced by two rāʾs); we point the printed letters. الْمَعَاجِين are electuaries, medicinal pastes mixed with honey or sugar. السُّكَّر is sugar; the shadda is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَقَامَتْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ شُهُورًا وَهِيَ مَحْجُوبَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-aqāmat ʿalā dhālika shuhūran wa-hiya maḥjūbatun
sentences.l: and she stayed upon that for months, she veiled.
sentences.i: She stayed so for months, shut away from sight.
sentences.n: أَقَامَتْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ, "she persisted in that": she kept to her seclusion.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ قَدْ بَرَدَتْ نَارُهُ وَانْطَفَأَ شَوْقُهُ مِنْهَا وَصَبَرَ عَنْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma anna al-malika qad baradat nāruhu wa-inṭafaʾa shawquhu minhā wa-ṣabara ʿanhā
sentences.l: Then that the king, his fire had cooled and his longing for her was put out, and he was patient away from her.
sentences.i: Then the king's fire cooled, his longing for her was put out, and he bore being apart from her.
sentences.n: ثُمَّ أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ قَدْ بَرَدَتْ نَارُهُ: the noun after أَنَّ is followed by a full clause with its own subject ("the king, his fire had cooled"). The أ of وَانْطَفَأَ is printed by the edition and stays precomposed. صَبَرَ عَنْ is "to do without, endure the absence of".

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ قَدْ عَلِقَتْ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat qad ʿaliqat minhu
sentences.l: And she had conceived from him.
sentences.i: But she had conceived by him.
sentences.n: عَلِقَتْ مِنْ is "to conceive by" (literally, to cling).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَرَّتْ عَلَيْهَا أَشْهُرُ الْحَمْلِ ظَهَرَ حَمْلُهَا وَكَبُرَتْ بَطْنُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā marrat ʿalayhā ashhuru al-ḥamli ẓahara ḥamluhā wa-kaburat baṭnuhā
sentences.l: And when the months of the pregnancy had passed over her, her pregnancy appeared, and her belly grew-big.
sentences.i: As the months of pregnancy passed over her, her condition showed and her belly grew large.
sentences.n: The verb كَبُرَتْ is feminine to agree with بَطْن, which is treated as feminine here. The sentence is cut off here; the next unit carries the rest. The shadda on مَرَّتْ is printed.

sentences.t: وَضَاقَتِ الدُّنْيَا بِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ḍāqati al-dunyā bihā
sentences.l: And the world grew narrow with her,
sentences.i: And the world closed in upon her,
sentences.n: A fragment: the sentence began in the preceding lines. ضَاقَ بِهَا الدُّنْيَا is the idiom for being at one's wits' end, with بِـ marking the person affected.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِجَارِيَتِهَا مَرْجَانَةَ أعْلَمِي أنَّ الْقَوْمَ مَا ظَلَمُونِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-jāriyatihā Marjānata iʿlamī anna al-qawma mā ẓalamūnī
sentences.l: And she said to her girl Marjāna: Know that the people did not wrong me,
sentences.i: Then she said to her maid Marjāna, "Know that those people did me no wrong;

sentences.t: وَإنَّمَا أنَا الْجَانِيَةُ عَلَى نَفْسِي حَيْثُ فَارَقْتُ أبِي وَأمِّى وَمَمْلَكَتِى
sentences.tr: wa-innamā anā al-jāniyatu ʿalā nafsī ḥaythu fāraqtu abī wa-ummī wa-mamlakatī
sentences.l: and only I am the wrong-doer upon my self, since I left my father and my mother and my kingdom,
sentences.i: it is I who have wronged myself, in leaving my father, my mother and my kingdom.
sentences.n: The edition prints ى for the final yā' of وَأمِّى and وَمَمْلَكَتِى (and later عِنْدِى, فِى); the spelling is kept.

sentences.t: وَأنَا قَدْ كَرِهْتُ الْحَيَاةَ وَانْكَسَرَتْ هِمَّتِى وَمَا بَقِيَ عِنْدِى مِنَ الْهِمَّةِ وَلَا مِنَ الْقُوَّةِ شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: wa-anā qad karihtu al-ḥayāta wa-inkasarat himmatī wa-mā baqiya ʿindī mina al-himmati wa-lā mina al-quwwati shayʾun
sentences.l: and I have indeed come-to-hate life, and my resolve has broken, and there has not remained with me of the resolve, nor of the strength, anything,
sentences.i: I have come to hate life; my spirit is broken, and no resolve or strength is left in me.

sentences.t: وَكُنْتُ إذَا رَكِبْتُ جَوَادِي أقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ وَأنَا الْآنَ لَا أقْدِرُ عَلَى الرُّكُوبِ
sentences.tr: wa-kuntu idhā rakibtu jawādī aqdiru ʿalayhi wa-anā al-ān lā aqdiru ʿalā al-rukūbi
sentences.l: and I used to, when I rode my steed, be able upon it; and I now am not able upon riding,
sentences.i: I used to mount my steed and master it, but now I cannot even ride.
sentences.n: كُنْتُ ... أقْدِرُ "I used to be able": kāna with a present verb gives the habitual past. The آ in الْآنَ is printed by the edition and stays precomposed.

sentences.t: وَإنِّي مَتَى وَلَدْتُ عِنْدَهُمْ صِرْتُ مُعَيَّرَةً عِنْدَ جَوَارِي
sentences.tr: wa-innī matā waladtu ʿindahum ṣirtu muʿayyaratan ʿinda jawārī
sentences.l: and indeed I, whenever I give birth among them, become one-reproached in the presence of my girls,
sentences.i: And if I give birth among them, I shall become a reproach before my own maids.
sentences.n: مَتَى here is "if / as soon as", not "when?". مُعَيَّرَة is one who is taunted or shamed (عَيَّرَ).

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ مَنْ فِى الْقَصْرِ يَعْلَمُ أنَّهُ أخَذَ وَجْهِي سِفَاحًا
sentences.tr: wa-kullu man fī al-qaṣri yaʿlamu annahu akhadha wajhī sifāḥan
sentences.l: and everyone who is in the palace knows that he took my face in fornication,
sentences.i: and everyone in the palace knows that he took me outside marriage.
sentences.n: "Took my face" is an idiom for taking one's honour or virginity; سِفَاحًا is unlawful intercourse, outside wedlock (in contrast to نِكَاح). The queen is speaking of the king's rape of her while she was drugged.

sentences.t: وَأنَا إذَا رَجَعْتُ لِأبِي بِأَيِّ وَجْهٍ ألْقَاهُ وَبِأَيِّ وَجْهٍ أرْجِعُ إلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā idhā rajaʿtu li-abī bi-ayyi wajhin alqāhu wa-bi-ayyi wajhin arjiʿu ilayhi
sentences.l: and I, if I return to my father, with what face do I meet him, and with what face do I return to him?
sentences.i: And if I go back to my father, with what face can I meet him, and with what face return to him?

sentences.t: وَمَا أحْسَنَ قَوْلَ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā aḥsana qawla al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: and how-good is the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: How well the poet put it:

sentences.t: بِمَ التَّعَلُّلُ لَا اَهْلٌ وَلَا وَطَنُ * وَلَا نَدِيمَ وَلَا كَأْسٌ وَلَا سَكَنُ
sentences.tr: bima al-taʿallulu lā ahlun wa-lā waṭanu * wa-lā nadīma wa-lā kaʾsun wa-lā sakanu
sentences.l: By what is the diversion? No kin and no homeland * and no boon-companion and no cup and no dwelling-place!
sentences.i: What comfort is left? No kin, no homeland, no friend to drink with, no cup, and no place of rest.
sentences.n: The print points this line, and we copy it as printed. اَهْلٌ (with fatḥa on the alif), وَلَا نَدِيمَ (accusative without tanwīn, the "no" of absolute negation) and the rhyme in -nu are as printed; سَكَنُ and وَطَنُ are pointed without tanwīn for the rhyme. بِمَ is بِمَا with the alif dropped after the preposition.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا مَرْجَانَةُ الْأمْرُ أمْرُكِ وَأنَا فِي طَوْعِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā Marjānatu al-amru amruki wa-anā fī ṭawʿiki
sentences.l: And Marjāna said to her: The command is your command, and I am in your obedience.
sentences.i: Marjāna said to her, "The command is yours, and I am at your will."

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أرِيدُ السَّاعَةَ أنْ أخْرُجَ سِرًّا بِحَيْثُ لَايَعْلَمُ بِي أحَدٌ غَيْرُكِ وَأسَافِرَ إلَى أبِي وَأمِّى
sentences.tr: fa-qālat urīdu al-sāʿata an akhruja sirran bi-ḥaythu lā-yaʿlamu bī aḥadun ghayruki wa-usāfira ilā abī wa-ummī
sentences.l: And she said: I want, the hour, that I go out secretly, such that there knows of me no one other than you, and that I travel to my father and my mother,
sentences.i: She said, "I want to leave this very hour, in secret, so that no one but you knows of it, and to travel to my father and mother;
sentences.n: لَايَعْلَمُ is printed as one word, لَا and the verb run together. بِحَيْثُ is "in such a way that", and it takes the indicative. The shadda on سِرًّا is printed in the edition.

sentences.t: فَإنَّ اللَّحْمَ إذَا أنْتَنَ مَا لَهُ إلَّا أهْلُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-laḥma idhā antana mā lahu illā ahluhu
sentences.l: for indeed the flesh, when it has stunk, has nothing but its own people,
sentences.i: for when flesh has spoiled, only its own kin will bear it.
sentences.n: A proverb: even rotten meat belongs to its own household. She means that she can only go back to her own family, however shamed.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ بِي مَايُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhu yafʿalu bī mā-yurīdu
sentences.l: and God does with me what He wills.
sentences.i: and God will do with me what He wills."
sentences.n: مَايُرِيدُ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا نِعْمَ مَا تَفْعَلِينَ أيَّتُهَا الْمَلِكَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā niʿma mā tafʿalīna ayyatuhā al-malikatu
sentences.l: And she said to her: How excellent is what you do, O queen!
sentences.i: She said, "What you do is well done, O queen."
sentences.n: نِعْمَ مَا is the praise formula: "excellent is what ...".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إنَّهَا جَهَّزَتْ أحْوَالَهَا وَكَتَمَتْ سِرَّهَا وَصَبَرَتْ أيَّا مَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahā jahhazat aḥwālahā wa-katamat sirrahā wa-ṣabarat ayyā mā
sentences.l: Then that she made-ready her affairs, and concealed her secret, and was patient days, [ayyā mā]
sentences.i: Then she made ready her affairs, kept her secret, and waited some days,
sentences.n: اَيَّا مَا is printed as two words but is plainly أيَّامًا, "days"; we point the two printed words so that they read together.

sentences.t: حَتَّى خَرَجَ الْمَلِكُ لِلصَّيْدِ وَالْقَنْصِ
sentences.tr: ḥattā kharaja al-maliku li-al-ṣaydi wa-al-qanṣi
sentences.l: until the king went out to the hunting and the chase,
sentences.i: until the king went out hunting,

sentences.t: وَخَرَجَ وَالِدُهُ شَرْكَانُ إلَى الْقِلَاعِ لِيُقِيمَ بِهَا مُدَّةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-kharaja wāliduhu Sharkānu ilā al-qilāʿi li-yuqīma bihā muddatan mina al-zamāni
sentences.l: and there went out his father Sharkān to the fortresses, in order that he stay in them a span of time.
sentences.i: and his son Sharkān went out to the fortresses, to stay there for a while.
sentences.n: The print has وَالِدُهُ, "his father", where the sense wants وَلَدُهُ, "his son": Sharkān is the king's son. The literal layer keeps the printed word.

sentences.t: فَأقْبَلَتْ أبْرِيزَةُ عَلَى جَارِيَتِهَا مَرْجَانَةَ وَقَالَتْ لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-aqbalat Abrīzatu ʿalā jāriyatihā Marjānata wa-qālat lahā
sentences.l: And Abrīza turned toward her girl Marjāna and said to her:
sentences.i: Abrīza turned to her maid Marjāna and said,

sentences.t: أرِيدُأنْ أسَافِرَ فِي هَذِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَلَكِنْ كَيْفَ أصْنَعُ فِى الْمَقَادِيرِ
sentences.tr: urīdu-an usāfira fī hādhi al-laylati wa-lākin kayfa aṣnaʿu fī al-maqādīri
sentences.l: I want that I travel in this night; but how shall I act in the decrees?
sentences.i: "I want to leave tonight, but what am I to do against what is decreed?
sentences.n: اريدان is two words run together (أرِيدُ + أنْ), and هَذِ is printed for هَذِهِ. فِى الْمَقَادِيرِ means "against the decrees (of fate)".

sentences.t: وَقَدْ حَسِيتُ بِالطَّلْقِ وَالْوِلَادَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ḥasaytu bi-al-ṭalqi wa-al-wilādati
sentences.l: for I have felt the labour-pains and the birthing.
sentences.i: I have felt the pangs of labour already.
sentences.n: حَسِيتُ is a Middle Arabic form (Classical أحْسَسْتُ), and the verb takes بِـ for the thing felt.

sentences.t: وَإنْ قَعَدْتُ خَمْسَةَ أيَّامٍ أوْ أرْبَعَةً وَضَعْتُ هُنَا وَلَمْ أقْدِرْ أنْ أرُوحَ بِلَادِي
sentences.tr: wa-in qaʿadtu khamsata ayyāmin aw arbaʿatan waḍaʿtu hunā wa-lam aqdir an arūḥa bilādī
sentences.l: And if I sit five days or four, I will give birth here, and I shall not be able to go to my land;
sentences.i: If I stay five days or four, I shall give birth here and be unable to reach my own country.
sentences.n: أرُوحَ بِلَادِي "go (to) my land" uses رَاحَ with a direct object, a colloquial feature; وَضَعْتُ is a past tense in the sense of a conditional result.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا مَا كَانَ مَكْتُوبًا عَلَى جَبِينِي
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā mā kāna maktūban ʿalā jabīnī
sentences.l: and this is what was written upon my brow.
sentences.i: This is what was written on my brow.
sentences.n: The brow is where fate is imagined to be written.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَفَكَّرَتْ سَاعَةً وَقَالَتْ لِمَرْجَانَةَ أنْظُرِي لَنَا رَجُلًا نُسَافِرُ وَإيَّاهُ وَيَخْدِمُنَا فِي الطَّرِيقِ
sentences.tr: thumma tafakkarat sāʿatan wa-qālat li-Marjānata unẓurī lanā rajulan nusāfiru wa-iyyāhu wa-yakhdimunā fī al-ṭarīqi
sentences.l: Then she thought an hour, and said to Marjāna: Look for us a man, we travel and him, and he serves us on the road,
sentences.i: Then she thought a while and said to Marjāna, "Find us a man to travel with, who will serve us on the road,
sentences.n: وَإيَّاهُ is "and him", the object pronoun, used for "with him".

sentences.t: فَإنِّي لَيْسَ لِي قُوَّةٌ عَلَى حَمْلِ السِّلَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-innī laysa lī quwwatun ʿalā ḥamli al-silāḥi
sentences.l: for indeed I, there is not to me strength for the bearing of arms.
sentences.i: for I have no strength to bear arms."

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ مَرْجَانَةُ وَاللَّهِ يَاسَيِّدَتِي مَا أعْرِفُ غَيْرَ عَبْدٍ أسْوَدَ أسْمُهُ الْغَضْبَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat Marjānatu wa-Allāhi yā-sayyidatī mā aʿrifu ghayra ʿabdin aswada ismuhu al-Ghaḍbānu
sentences.l: And Marjāna said: By God, O my lady, I know no one other than a slave, black, his name al-Ghaḍbān,
sentences.i: Marjāna said, "By God, my lady, I know of no one but a black slave named al-Ghaḍbān,
sentences.n: يَاسَيِّدَتِي is printed with the vocative and noun run together.

sentences.t: وَهُمُو مِنْ عَبِيدِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-humū min ʿabīdi al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni
sentences.l: and humū is of the slaves of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān,
sentences.i: who is one of the slaves of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān,
sentences.n: وَهُمُو is odd. It may be a misprint for وَهُوَ ("and he"), or the old long form هُمُو of the pronoun used for a singular; we point it as printed.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ شُجَاعٌ مُلَازِمٌ لِبَابِ قَصْرِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-huwa shujāʿun mulāzimun li-bābi qaṣrinā
sentences.l: and he is brave, one-attached to the door of our palace,
sentences.i: a brave man who keeps always at the door of our palace.

sentences.t: وَأمَرَهُ الْمَلِكُ أنْ يَخْدِمَنَا وَقَدْ غَمَرْنَاهُ بِإحْسَانِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-amarahu al-maliku an yakhdimanā wa-qad ghamarnāhu bi-iḥsāninā
sentences.l: and the king commanded him that he serve us, and we have flooded him with our beneficence.
sentences.i: The king commanded him to serve us, and we have showered him with kindness.
sentences.n: The subject of أمَرَهُ is the king; the slave is ʿUmar's, but placed by him in the household.

sentences.t: فَهَا أنَا أخْرُجُ إلَيْهِ وَأكَلِّمُهُ فِي هَذَا الْأمْرِ وَأعِدُهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-hā anā akhruju ilayhi wa-ukallimuhu fī hādhā al-amri wa-aʿiduhu bi-shayʾin mina al-māli
sentences.l: So behold, I go out to him and speak to him in this matter and promise him with a thing of money,
sentences.i: So I shall go out to him, speak to him about this, and promise him some money,
sentences.n: وَعَدَ بِـ "promise (someone) something" takes the thing with بِـ.

sentences.t: وَأقُولُ لَهُ إذَا أرَدْتَ الْمُقَامَ عِنْدَنَا أزَوِّجُكَ بِمَنْ شِئْتَ
sentences.tr: wa-aqūlu lahu idhā aradta al-muqāma ʿindanā uzawwijuka bi-man shiʾta
sentences.l: and I say to him: If you want residence with us, I will marry you to whom you please.
sentences.i: and tell him that if he will stay with us, I shall marry him to whomever he likes.
sentences.n: The shadda on أزَوِّجُكَ is printed. زَوَّجَ بِـ means "to give in marriage to".

sentences.t: وَكَانَ قَدْ ذَكَرَنِي قَبْلَ الْيَوْمِ أنَّهُ كَانَ يَقْطَعُ الطَّرِيقَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna qad dhakaranī qabla al-yawmi annahu kāna yaqṭaʿu al-ṭarīqa
sentences.l: And he had indeed mentioned me, before today, that he used to cut the road.
sentences.i: He had told me before today that he used to be a highwayman.
sentences.n: ذَكَرَنِي is printed with the object pronoun on the person, for ذَكَرَ لِي ("he told me"); it could also be read as ذَكَّرَنِي ("he reminded me"). We point it as printed. قَطَعَ الطَّرِيقَ is "to waylay".

sentences.t: فَإنْ هُوَطَا وَعَنَا بَلَغْنَا مُرَادَنَا وَوَصَلْنَا إلَى بِلَادِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-in huwaṭā waʿanā balaghnā murādanā wa-waṣalnā ilā bilādinā
sentences.l: So if huwaṭā waʿanā, we shall reach our desire and arrive at our land.
sentences.i: If he proves loyal to us, we shall reach our goal and come to our own country.
sentences.n: هُوَطَا وَعَنَا is misdivided in print and is surely هُوَ طَاوَعَنَا, "he obeys us" (طَاوَعَ, "to be compliant"). We point the two printed words as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا نَادِيهِ عِنْدِي حَتَّى أحَدِّثَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā nādīhi ʿindī ḥattā uḥaddithahu
sentences.l: And she said to her: Call him to me, until I speak to him.
sentences.i: She said to her, "Call him to me, that I may speak with him."

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتْ لَهُ مَرْجَانَةُ وَنَادَتْ يَا غَضْبَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajat lahu Marjānatu wa-nādat yā Ghaḍbānu
sentences.l: And Marjāna went out to him and called: O Ghaḍbān,
sentences.i: Marjāna went out to him and called, "Ghaḍbān,

sentences.t: قَدْ أسْعَدَكَ اللَّهُ إنْ قَبِلْتَ مِنْ سَيِّدَتِي مَاتَقُولُهُ لَكَ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: qad asʿadaka Allāhu in qabilta min sayyidatī mā-taqūluhu laka mina al-kalāmi
sentences.l: God has indeed made you fortunate, if you accept from my lady what she says to you of speech,
sentences.i: God has favoured you if you accept what my lady says to you,
sentences.n: مَاتَقُولُهُ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: وَأخَذَتْ بِيَدِهِ وَأقْبَلَتْ بِهِ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhat bi-yadihi wa-aqbalat bihi ʿalayhā
sentences.l: and she took him by his hand and brought him to her.
sentences.i: and she took him by the hand and brought him to her."
sentences.n: The subject changes: after her words to him, Marjāna takes him by the hand to the queen. أَخَذَ بِيَدِهِ is "to take by the hand".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا قَبَّلَ يَدَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā rāʾahā qabbala yadayhā
sentences.l: And when he saw her he kissed her two hands,
sentences.i: When he saw her he kissed her hands,
sentences.n: The آ in رَآهَا is printed by the edition and stays precomposed.

sentences.t: فَحِينَ رَأَتْهُ نَفَرَ قَلْبُهَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥīna raʾathu nafara qalbuhā minhu
sentences.l: but when she saw him her heart shrank from him.
sentences.i: but when she saw him her heart shrank from him.
sentences.n: The أ in رَأَتْهُ is printed by the edition and stays precomposed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ فِي نَفْسِهَا إنَّ الضَّرُورَةَ لَهَا أحْكَامٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat fī nafsihā inna al-ḍarūrata lahā aḥkāmun
sentences.l: And she said in her self: Indeed necessity has rulings.
sentences.i: She said to herself, "Necessity has its own laws."
sentences.n: The saying is the Arabic counterpart of "necessity knows no law".

sentences.t: وَأقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ تُحَدِّثُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbalat ʿalayhi tuḥaddithuhu
sentences.l: and she turned toward him, speaking to him.
sentences.i: and she turned to him and spoke to him.
sentences.n: A fragment: what she says is carried by the following lines. تُحَدِّثُهُ is a present verb used as a circumstantial clause.

sentences.t: وَقَلْبُهَا نَافِرٌ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qalbuhā nāfirun minhu
sentences.l: and her heart averse from him,
sentences.i: though her heart shrank from him,
sentences.n: This is a fragment: a circumstantial clause ("her heart being averse from him") that hangs on the sentence just before it, where the queen speaks to the slave al-Ghaḍbān while loathing him.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا غَضْبَانُ هَلْ فِيكَ مُسَاعَدَةٌ لَنَا عَلَى غَدَرَاتِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu yā Ghaḍbānu hal fīka musāʿadatun lanā ʿalā ghadarāti al-zamāni
sentences.l: and she said to him: O Ghaḍbān, is there in you help for us against the treacheries of the time?
sentences.i: and she said to him, "O Ghaḍbān, is there in you any help for us against the treacheries of fate?"
sentences.n: غَدَرَات is the plural of غَدْرَة, "an act of treachery"; الزَّمَان, "time", is fate, the turns of fortune. The name غَضْبَان means "angry"; here it is the slave's name.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا أَظْهَرْتُكَ عَلَى أَمْرِي تَكُونُ كَاتِمًا لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā aẓhartuka ʿalā amrī takūnu kātiman lahu
sentences.l: so if I show-you-openly upon my affair, will you be a concealer of it?
sentences.i: If I let you in on my secret, will you keep it hidden?
sentences.n: أَظْهَرَهُ عَلَى is "to let someone see, make known to someone". تَكُونُ كَاتِمًا, "you will be a concealer", is a periphrasis for "you will conceal", and the clause carries the force of a question.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ الْعَبْدُ إِلَيْهَا مَلَكَتْ قَلْبَهُ وَعَشِقَهَا لِوَقْتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara al-ʿabdu ilayhā malakat qalbahu wa-ʿashiqahā li-waqtihi
sentences.l: And when the slave looked at her, she possessed his heart, and he fell-passionately-in-love-with her at his moment.
sentences.i: When the slave looked at her, she took possession of his heart, and he fell madly in love with her on the spot.
sentences.n: لِوَقْتِهِ, "at his moment", is an idiom for "at once, on the spot"; لِـ here marks the time.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ غَيْرَأَنَّهُ قَالَ يَاسَيِّدَتِي إِنْ أَمَرْتِنِي بِشَيْءٍ لَا أَخْرُجُ عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yumkinhu ghayra annahu qāla yā-sayyidatī in amartinī bi-shayʾin lā akhruju ʿanhu
sentences.l: And it was not possible for him other than that he said: O my lady, if you command me with anything, I shall not go out from it.
sentences.i: He could do nothing but say, "My lady, if you command me in anything, I will not depart from it."
sentences.n: The edition prints غيرانه as one word: غَيْرَ, "other than", run together with أَنَّهُ, "that he"; we point it as printed, with no space. فَلَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ غَيْرَ أَنْ is a stock phrase, "he could do nothing but". يَاسَيِّدَتِي is likewise printed as one word, vocative يَا plus سَيِّدَتِي. أَمَرَ بِ is "to command something".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أُرِيدُ مِنْكَ السَّاعَةَ أَنْ تَأْخُذَنِي وَتَأْخُذَ جَارِيَتِي هَذِهِ وَتَشُدَّ لَنَا رَاحِلَتَيْنِ وَرَأْسَيْ خَيْلٍ مِنْ خُيُولِ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu urīdu minka al-sāʿata an taʾkhudhanī wa-taʾkhudha jāriyatī hādhihi wa-tashudda lanā rāḥilatayni wa-raʾsay khaylin min khuyūli al-maliki
sentences.l: And she said to him: I want from you the hour that you take me and take this my girl and tie for us two riding-camels and two heads of horses from the horses of the king,
sentences.i: She said to him, "What I want of you this very hour is that you take me and this maid of mine, and saddle for us two riding-camels and two horses from the king's horses,
sentences.n: السَّاعَةَ, "the hour", in the accusative is "right now". شَدَّ لَنَا is "to tie on (the gear) for us", that is, to saddle and load. رَأْسَيْ خَيْلٍ, "two heads of horses", counts the horses the way a herdsman does. The shadda printed on تَشُدَّ is kept.

sentences.t: وَتَجْعَلَ عَلَى كُلِّ فَرَسٍ خُرْجًا مِنَ الْمَالِ وَشَيْأً مِنَ الزَّادِ وَتَرْحَلَ مَعَنَا إِلَى بِلَادِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-tajʿala ʿalā kulli farasin khurjan mina al-māli wa-shayʾan mina al-zādi wa-tarḥala maʿanā ilā bilādinā
sentences.l: and put upon every horse a saddlebag of the money and something of the provisions, and journey with us to our lands,
sentences.i: and put on every horse a saddlebag of money and some provisions, and travel with us to our country.
sentences.n: فَرَس is a horse of either sex. The edition's شَيْأً is a variant spelling of شَيْئًا, "something"; its أ is printed by the edition and stays as a full letter.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ أَقَمْتَ عِنْدَنَا زَوَّجْتُكَ بِمَنْ تَخْتَارُهَا مِنْ جَوَارِيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-in aqamta ʿindanā zawwajtuka bi-man takhtāruhā min jawāriyya
sentences.l: And if you stay with us, I shall marry-you to whom you choose her from my girls,
sentences.i: If you stay with us, I will marry you to whichever of my maids you choose,
sentences.n: بِمَنْ تَخْتَارُهَا has a resumptive pronoun ("whom you choose her"), which Classical Arabic would not repeat. زَوَّجَهُ بِ is "to marry him to" (a woman). The shadda printed on جَوَارِيَّ is kept; it is the plural جَوَارٍ plus "my".

sentences.t: وَإِنْ طَلَبْتَ الرُّجُوعَ إِلَى بِلَادِلَ زَوَّجْنَاكَ وَأَعْطَيْنَاكَ مَا تُحِبُّ إِلَى بِلَادِكَ بَعْدَ أَنْ تَأْخُذَ مَا يَكْفِيكَ مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-in ṭalabta al-rujūʿa ilā bilādila zawwajnāka wa-aʿṭaynāka mā tuḥibbu ilā bilādika baʿda an taʾkhudha mā yakfīka mina al-māli
sentences.l: and if you seek the returning to the lands of [bilādila], we shall marry-you and give you what you love, to your land, after that you take what suffices you of the money.
sentences.i: and if you wish to return to your own country, we will marry you and give you what you desire, and send you to your land after you have taken as much money as will suffice you.
sentences.n: بِلَادِلَ is a misprint, most likely for بِلَادِكَ, "your land", which the end of the sentence has in full; we point the printed letters and the idiomatic line takes it as "your country". The sentence is also compressed: "give you what you love, to your land" means send you on your way with what you wish.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْغَضْبَانُ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ فَرِحَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا وَقَالَ يَاسَيِّدَتِي إِنِّي أَخْدُمُكُمَا بِعُيُونِي وَأَمْضِي مَعَكُمَا وَأَشُدُّ لَكُمَا الْخَيْلَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-Ghaḍbānu dhālika al-kalāma fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan wa-qāla yā-sayyidatī innī akhdumukumā bi-ʿuyūnī wa-amḍī maʿakumā wa-ashuddu lakumā al-khayla
sentences.l: And when al-Ghaḍbān heard that speech, he rejoiced a severe rejoicing, and said: O my lady, indeed I serve you two with my eyes, and I go on with you two, and I tie for you two the horses.
sentences.i: When al-Ghaḍbān heard that, he was filled with joy and said, "My lady, I will serve you both with my eyes, and go with you, and make the horses ready for you."
sentences.n: بِعُيُونِي, "with my eyes", is a courtly formula of eager service ("gladly, with all my heart"). The dual pronoun كُمَا addresses the queen and her maid.

sentences.t: فَمَضَى وَهُوَ فَرْحَانُ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ قَدْ بَلَغْتُ مَا أُرِيدُ مِنْهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-maḍā wa-huwa farḥānu wa-qāla fī nafsihi qad balaghtu mā urīdu minhumā
sentences.l: And he went off, and he rejoicing, and said in his self: I have reached what I want from the two of them.
sentences.i: He went off rejoicing, and said to himself, "I have got from the two of them all I wanted.
sentences.n: فَرْحَان, "glad", is a diptote, so it takes no tanwīn. فِي نَفْسِهِ, "in his self", means "to himself" (in his own mind).

sentences.t: وَإِنْ لَمْ تُطَا وَعَانِي قَتَلْتُهُمَا وَأَخَذْتُ مَا مَعَهُمَا مِنَ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-in lam tuṭā waʿānī qataltuhumā wa-akhadhtu mā maʿahumā mina al-māli
sentences.l: And if they do not [tuṭā waʿānī], I shall have killed the two of them and taken what is with the two of them of the money.
sentences.i: If they do not do my will, I will kill them both and take the money they have with them."
sentences.n: تُطَا وَعَانِي is printed as two words and reads best as one, لَمْ تُطَاوِعَانِي, "they two do not obey me" (طَاوَعَ, "to comply with"), with the dual ending ـانِ kept after لَمْ, a Middle Arabic feature, and a stray space. We point the two printed pieces as they stand. The two perfects after إِنْ, "I shall have killed ... and taken", state the threat as a thing already settled.

sentences.t: وَأَضْمَرَ ذَلِكَ فِي سِرِّهِ ثُمَّ مَضَى وَعَادَ وَمَعَهُ رَاحِلَتَانِ وَثَلٰثُ رُؤُسٍ مِنَ الْخَيْلِ وَهُوَ رَاكِبٌ عَلَى أَحَدِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-aḍmara dhālika fī sirrihi thumma maḍā wa-ʿāda wa-maʿahu rāḥilatāni wa-thalāthu ruʾusin mina al-khayli wa-huwa rākibun ʿalā aḥadihim
sentences.l: And he concealed that in his secret, then went off and returned, and with him two riding-camels and three heads of the horses, and he riding upon one of them.
sentences.i: He hid that in his heart, then went off and came back with two riding-camels and three horses, himself mounted on one of them.
sentences.n: ثَلٰثُ is the edition's defective spelling of ثَلَاثُ, "three" (so with the dagger alif), and رُؤُسٍ its short spelling of رُؤُوسٍ, "heads". The count fits the story: two horses for the women, one for the slave. أَحَدِهِمْ is a masculine plural pronoun for the horses, as Middle Arabic often does with non-human plurals.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ وَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهَا فَرَسًا فَرَكِبَتْ وَاحِدًا وَأَرْكَبَتْ مَرْجَانَةَ وَاحِدًا وَهِيَ مُتَوَجِّعَةٌ مِنَ الطَّلْقِ وَلَا تَمَالَكُ نَفْسَهَا مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الْوَجَعِ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbala ʿalā al-malikati Abrīzata wa-qaddama ilayhā farasan fa-rakibat wāḥidan wa-arkabat Marjānata wāḥidan wa-hiya mutawajjiʿatun mina al-ṭalqi wa-lā tamālaku nafsahā min kathrati al-wajaʿi
sentences.l: And he turned toward the queen Abrīza and presented to her a horse, and she rode one and had Marjāna ride one, and she in pain from the labour-pangs, and not holding herself from the abundance of the ache.
sentences.i: He turned to Queen Abrīza and brought her a horse; she mounted one and set Marjāna on another, though she was racked with labour pains and could scarcely contain herself for the pain.
sentences.n: الطَّلْق is the pangs of childbirth. تَمَالَكُ is read as تَتَمَالَكُ with one تَ dropped, "she does not control herself"; with نَفْسَهَا the verb means "to restrain oneself".

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ مُسَافِرًا بِهِمَا فِي عَرْصَةِ الْجِبَالِ لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا إِلَى أَنْ بَقِيَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ بِلَادِهَا يَوْمٌ وَاحِدٌ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla musāfiran bihimā fī ʿaraṣati al-jibāli laylan wa-nahāran ilā an baqiya baynahā wa-bayna bilādihā yawmun wāḥidun
sentences.l: And he did not cease travelling with the two of them in the open-space of the mountains night and day, until there remained between her and her lands one day.
sentences.i: He kept travelling with them through the mountain wastes by night and by day, until only one day lay between her and her country.
sentences.n: عَرْصَة is an open tract or courtyard, here the open ground of the mountains. مُسَافِرًا بِهِمَا, "travelling with the two", means he takes them along.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَهَا الطَّلْقُ فَمَا قَدَرَتْ تُمْسِكُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾahā al-ṭalqu fa-mā qadarat tumsikuhu
sentences.l: And the labour came to her, and she was not able she hold it.
sentences.i: Then the pains came upon her, and she could not hold them back.
sentences.n: قَدَرَتْ تُمْسِكُهُ, "she was able, she holds it", drops أَنْ before the verb, a usual Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِلْغَضْبَانِ أَنْزِلْنِي فَقَدْ حَاشَنِي الطَّلْقُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-al-Ghaḍbāni anzilnī fa-qad ḥāshanī al-ṭalqu
sentences.l: And she said to al-Ghaḍbān: Lower me, for the labour has [ḥāshanī] me.
sentences.i: She said to al-Ghaḍbān, "Help me down, for the pains have come upon me."
sentences.n: حَاشَنِي is obscure, and may be a misprint for جَاشَنِي, "surged over me" (جَاشَ, of a rising swell); the pointing follows the printed letters, and the idiomatic line gives the sense, not the exact verb.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَتْ لِمَرْجَانَةَ انْزِ لِي وَاقْعُدِي تَحْتِي وَوَلِّدِينِي
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥat li-Marjānata inzi lī wa-uqʿudī taḥtī wa-wallidīnī
sentences.l: And she cried to Marjāna: Come-down [for] me, and sit beneath me, and deliver me.
sentences.i: and she cried to Marjāna, "Get down, sit beneath me and deliver my child!"
sentences.n: انْزِ لِي is printed with a space: it is the feminine imperative اِنْزِلِي, "come down", with the final ـلِي split off as if it were لِي, "to me". We point the two printed pieces as they stand. وَلِّدِينِي is "act as midwife to me" (وَلَّدَ, "to cause to give birth").

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَزَلَتْ مَرْجَانَةُ مِنْ فَوْقِ فَرَسِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika nazalat Marjānatu min fawqi farasihā
sentences.l: And at that, Marjāna descended from above her horse,
sentences.i: At that Marjāna got down from her horse,

sentences.t: وَنَزَلَ الْغَضْبَانُ مِنْ فَوْقِ فَرَسِهِ وَشَدَّ لِجَامَ الْفَرَسَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-nazala al-Ghaḍbānu min fawqi farasihi wa-shadda lijāma al-farasayni
sentences.l: and al-Ghaḍbān descended from above his horse and tied the bridle of the two horses,
sentences.i: and al-Ghaḍbān got down from his and made fast the bridles of the two horses,
sentences.n: لِجَامَ الْفَرَسَيْنِ, "the bridle of the two horses", is a singular for two animals: the two the women had been riding.

sentences.t: وَنَزَلَتِ الْمَلِكَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ مِنْ فَوْقِ الْجَوَادِ وَهِيَ غَائِبَةٌ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا مِنْ شِدَّةِ الطَّلْقِ
sentences.tr: wa-nazalati al-malikatu Abrīzatu min fawqi al-jawādi wa-hiya ghāʾibatun ʿani al-dunyā min shiddati al-ṭalqi
sentences.l: and the queen Abrīza descended from above the steed, and she absent from the world from the severity of the labour.
sentences.i: and Queen Abrīza got down from her steed, half unconscious of the world from the violence of her pains.
sentences.n: غَائِبَةٌ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا, "absent from the world", means she was dazed with pain, nearly senseless. الْجَوَاد, "the steed", is a fine horse.

sentences.t: وَحِينَ رَأَهَا الْغَضْبَانُ نَزَلَتْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ وَقَفَ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي وَجْهِ الْغَضْبَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥīna raʾahā al-Ghaḍbānu nazalat ʿalā al-arḍi waqafa al-shayṭānu fī wajhi al-Ghaḍbāni
sentences.l: And when al-Ghaḍbān saw her, she had descended upon the ground, the devil stood in the face of al-Ghaḍbān.
sentences.i: When al-Ghaḍbān saw her down on the ground, Satan stood before him,
sentences.n: رَأَهَا is the edition's spelling of رَآهَا, "saw her", and its أ stays precomposed. نَزَلَتْ is a circumstantial clause ("she having descended"), joined without any و. وَقَفَ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي وَجْهِ is an idiom of temptation: Satan "stood in his face", got in his way and tempted him.

sentences.t: فَشَهَرَ حُسَامَهُ فِي وَجْهِهَا وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدَتِي ارْحَمِينِي بِوَصْلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-shahara ḥusāmahu fī wajhihā wa-qāla yā sayyidatī irḥamīnī bi-waṣlika
sentences.l: so he drew his sword in her face, and said: O my lady, have mercy on me with your joining.
sentences.i: and he drew his sword in her face and said, "My lady, have pity on me and give yourself to me!"
sentences.n: وَصْل, "joining", is union, here sexual union: he demands her body, sword drawn, while she is helpless in labour. ارْحَمِينِي بِ is "have mercy on me through", so the بِ introduces what he begs of her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ مَقَالَتَهُ الْتَفَتَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيَّ إِلَّا الْعَبِيدُ السُّودَانُ بَعْدَ مَا كُنْتُ لَا أَرْضَى بِالْمُلُوكِ الصَّنَادِيدِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat maqālatahu iltafatat ilayhi wa-qālat lahu mā baqiya ʿalayya illā al-ʿabīdu al-sūdānu baʿda mā kuntu lā arḍā bi-al-mulūki al-ṣanādīdi
sentences.l: And when she heard his saying, she turned to him and said to him: Nothing remains upon me except the slaves, the blacks, after I was one who was not satisfied with the kings, the chieftains.
sentences.i: When she heard his words she turned to him and said, "Nothing is left for me but black slaves, after I would not be content with mighty kings!"
sentences.n: مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيَّ إِلَّا, "nothing remains on me except", is a lament: this is all that is left to befall her. The shadda printed on عَلَيَّ is kept. الصَّنَادِيد are great lords and champions. The phrase الْعَبِيد السُّودَان, "the black slaves", is the text's own, in the queen's mouth.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād,
sentences.i: And the dawn overtook Shahrazād,

sentences.t: فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mu—bāḥi
sentences.l: and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: and she fell silent, leaving off the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The edition prints الْمُ—بَاحِ with a dash in the middle of the word; the word is the usual الْمُبَاحِ, "the permitted", of the closing formula, and we keep the dash as printed.
